author: copilot
body:
All gunicorn workers were failing the leader election on startup due to `get_db` not yet being defined when `_acquire_startup_leader_lock()` was called. Additionally, several query result consumers used tuple-style `row[0]` indexing incompatible with psycopg2's `RealDictCursor`, and MusicBrainz Lucene queries were not escaping special characters in artist/album names.

## Boot: `NameError: name 'get_db' is not defined`
`_acquire_startup_leader_lock()` was invoked at module load time ~200 lines before `get_db()` was defined. Every worker caught the `NameError` and degraded to non-leader, so no background schedulers ever started. Moved the entire startup election block to after `get_db()` and the `teardown_request` handler.

## `RealDictCursor` incompatible `row[0]` access
`get_db()` uses `cursor_factory=RealDictCursor`, so all rows are dicts. Integer-index access raises `KeyError: 0` rather than returning a value. The MBID collection check was silently failing with the cryptic warning `Could not perform MBID-based collection check for upcoming releases: 0` — that `0` is `str(KeyError(0))`.

Fixed 7 sites:
| Location | Query column | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `local_artists` set | bare `LOWER(COALESCE(...))` | added `AS artist_lower` alias |
| `canonical_artist` list | `AS canonical_artist` | `_row_get(row, "canonical_artist", 0)` |
| `existing_albums` (×2) | `album` | `_row_get(row, "album", 0)` |
| `queue_ids_to_delete` | `id` | `_row_get(row, "id", 0)` |
| `updated_ids` (RETURNING) | `id` | `_row_get(row, "id", 0)` |
| bookmarks page loop | named columns | `_row_get` for all 7 fields |
| MBID collection check | `musicbrainz_releasegroupid` | `_row_get(row, "musicbrainz_releasegroupid", 0)` |

## MusicBrainz Lucene query escaping
`_fetch_musicbrainz_releases` (text-search path) and `_search_musicbrainz_releasegroup_matches` were interpolating raw artist/album names into Lucene queries. Artists like `AC/DC` or `Guns N' Roses` produce malformed queries. `_escape_mb_phrase` was already imported but unused — now applied to both sites.

```python
# Before
query = f'artist:"{artist_name}" AND (primarytype:album OR primarytype:ep OR primarytype:single)'

# After
escaped_artist = _escape_mb_phrase(artist_name)
query = f'artist:"{escaped_artist}" AND (primarytype:album OR primarytype:ep OR primarytype:single)'
```

author: dglazkov
body:
## What
Adds hash-based URL routing to the Bees DevTools so that refreshing the page restores the active tab and selected item (log session, ticket, or event).

## Why
Previously, every page refresh reset the UI to the Jobs tab with no selection, forcing the user to re-navigate to whatever they were inspecting. This is especially painful for filesystem-backed tabs (Logs, Tickets, Events) that require re-granting directory access.

## Changes

### `packages/bees/web/src/data/router.ts` [NEW]
- Hash-based router (~60 lines): parses `#/{tab}/{id}` URLs, writes via `replaceState` to avoid history clutter

### `packages/bees/web/src/ui/app.ts`
- `restoreRoute()`: on page load, reads hash → sets tab → awaits store activation → restores selection
- `syncHash()`: after any user navigation (tab switch or sidebar click), writes current state to URL hash
- `activateCurrentStore()`: now re-reads the hash after filesystem access is granted, restoring the pending selection
- `hashchange` listener for manual URL edits

## Testing
- Open DevTools, switch to Logs/Tickets/Events tab, select an item → URL hash updates
- Refresh the page → same tab and item are restored
- For filesystem tabs without prior access: hash persists through the "Grant Access" flow

## Summary

Complete AI photo analysis service that integrates with the-mcculloughs.org:

### Features
- **Fetch & Analyze** - Downloads pending photos, analyzes with LLaVA vision model

# Process pending uploads
python scripts/run.py --limit 10

# Reprocess a specific photo
python scripts/run.py --shortcode ABC123 --debug

- "The Oul Man" / "The Oul Fella" → Edmund McCullough (Dad)

author: hegawy
body:
Adds a reporting endpoint that retrieves the most used promotions on the platform, including usage count, total discount given, and computed expiry status.

Endpoint:
GET /api/sales/promotions/top-used?limit={n}

Behavior:

Validates that the limit parameter is greater than 0.
Throws 400 BAD_REQUEST if limit is invalid.
Queries promotions joined with sale_promotions and groups by promotion.
Uses the promotion’s currentUses value as timesUsed.
Calculates totalDiscountGiven as the sum of sale_promotions.discount_applied for each promotion.
Orders results by timesUsed descending and limits the result size to n.
Maps each row to PromotionUsageDTO.
Computes the expired field in Java by comparing expiryDate with the current date and time.
Returns the list of most used promotions.
This allows platform managers to evaluate promotion performance and identify the most effective discounts.

Closes #90 

Reviewer: @KamalSaid58 @Medo4255

author: anticlub
body:
## ¿Qué hace este PR?
Integra las electrolineras de la API oficial de la DGT como un tipo de combustible más (`ELECTRICO`) dentro de la app, siguiendo la misma arquitectura existente. Las electrolineras aparecen en el mapa, listas por distancia y precio, favoritos y detalle de estación.

## Cambios principales
- Nuevo modelo `Electrolinera` y enum `ConnectorType` para los tipos de conector
- Parser XML (`RemoteDgtDataSource`) para el feed DATEX II de la DGT
- `EstacionRepository` que fusiona gasolineras y electrolineras en paralelo
- `FuelType.ELECTRICO` añadido — solo descarga el XML cuando está seleccionado
- `Gasolinera` extendida con campos eléctricos (`isElectric`, `operador`, `conectores`)
- Marcadores azules en el mapa con potencia máxima del cargador
- Lista por distancia muestra el conector de mayor potencia
- Lista "por precio" renombrada a "por cargador" para eléctrico, ordenada por potencia
- Pestaña "Precios" renombrada a "Cargadores" en el detalle, muestra tipo y potencia
- Pestaña "General" muestra el operador y oculta campos de precio/coste para eléctrico
- Búsqueda por municipio funciona también para electrolineras
- Logos de operadores eléctricos: Iberdrola, Endesa, Ionity, Zunder, Wenea, Acciona, Lidl, Mercadona, Ahorramas

## Cómo probar
1. Seleccionar combustible **Eléctrico** en preferencias
2. Verificar que el mapa muestra marcadores azules con potencia (ej: `350kW`)
3. Ir a **Por distancia** → lista de electrolineras con conector de mayor potencia
4. Ir a **Por cargador** → electrolineras ordenadas por potencia descendente
5. Pulsar una electrolinera → pestaña General muestra operador, pestaña Cargadores muestra conectores
6. Buscar un municipio → aparecen electrolineras en el mapa
7. Cambiar a combustible normal → todo funciona como antes

## Notas
- La primera carga con combustible eléctrico tarda ~60-90s (descarga XML de toda España ~12.000 estaciones). Pendiente de resolver en `refactor/cache-and-api-layer`.
- La rama se mergea a `develop` en lugar de `main` por la latencia de carga pendiente de optimizar.

body:
### Motivation

- Remove persona-specific visible UI text and legacy flag names from the universal embedded deck implementation so the generated decks are fully template-driven and persona-agnostic.
- Make special system UI visibility depend only on persona template flags and add builder-side tooling to generate persona-derived AI state greetings without moving generation into the runtime deck.

### Description

- Reworked template / build injection: added `AI_STATE_KEYS` and `<<<AI_STATE_GREETINGS_DECL>>>` placeholder, extended `build_deck_file()` to accept `ai_state_greetings` and inject `AI_STATE_GREETINGS = {...}` only when `AI_STATES_ENABLED` is true and greetings are provided; preserved `AI_STATES_ENABLED`, introduced `SUSPENSION_ENABLED`, and ensured `UI_SUSPENSION_LABEL` is injected with a `"Suspend"` fallback via `build_deck_file()` replacements.
- Removed persona-visible hardcoding from the embedded blob and re-encoded `_DECK_IMPL_B64`; the runtime now reads `AI_STATE_GREETINGS` when present and falls back to neutral defaults, and the embedded implementation includes the chat speaker spacing fix (`❩ ` / `❧ `) and inserted `pass`/safe branches where conditionals became empty.
- Added builder-side AI greeting subsystem entirely in `deck_builder.py`: functions to produce neutral defaults (`_neutral_state_greetings`), strict JSON extraction/coercion (`_extract_json_object`, `_coerce_state_greetings`), prompt builder (`_build_state_greeting_prompt`) and Ollama call path (`_request_state_greetings`); PersonaPanel UI added `Generate State Greetings`, `Regenerate`, `Use These`, and `Use Neutral Defaults` buttons with a preview showing all eight keys; approval flow stores approved greetings in builder session memory and reuses them during build.
- Wired UI → build pipeline: `ConnectionPanel` toggles generation enable, `DeckBuilderDialog` stores `_approved_state_greetings` and passes `ai_state_greetings` into `DeckSetupWorker`, and `build_deck_file()` injects the greetings declaration only when appropriate; `persona_Seraphel.txt` remained unchanged (it can provide `SUSPENSION_LABEL=Alcove` but does not become the default).

### Testing

- Compiled the modified builder: ran `python -m py_compile deck_builder.py` and it succeeded with no `SyntaxError`/`IndentationError`.
- Decoded the updated embedded implementation and validated forbidden strings and legacy flag names are absent and new template fields exist: ran a custom decode-and-scan script (forbidden-string check, template-field checks, chat spacing checks) and all checks passed.
- Verified the build-time plumbing and blob consumption: confirmed `<<<AI_STATE_GREETINGS_DECL>>>`, `AI_STATES_ENABLED`, `SUSPENSION_ENABLED`, and `UI_SUSPENSION_LABEL` injection paths exist and that `AI_STATE_GREETINGS` appears in the decoded blob consumption logic; these checks passed.
- Confirmed builder UI additions exist in `PersonaPanel` (buttons and preview) and that `DeckSetupWorker`/`build_deck_file()` accept and propagate `ai_state_greetings`; performed runtime-inspection scripts that located the new functions/UI symbols and they were present.

body:
### Motivation

- Eliminate ambiguous/undefined lifecycle values (e.g., "Unknown"/null) so every docket always has a valid lifecycle and UI never shows an empty/Unknown state.
- Make lifecycle handling resilient: recover to a sane default (`WL`) instead of throwing or returning `null` to avoid crashes and inconsistent API responses.

### Description

- Domain: `normalizeLifecycle` now returns `DocketLifecycle.WL` for unknown/empty input instead of throwing, and `assertValidLifecycleTransition` allows no-op transitions when `from === to` to avoid spurious errors. (`src/domain/docketLifecycle.js`).
- Model: `Case.model` lifecycle field now defaults to `WL`, is marked `required`, and uses a setter to normalize incoming values with `normalizeLifecycle` to prevent persisting `null`/invalid lifecycles. (`src/models/Case.model.js`).
- Repository: `CaseRepository` normalizes `lifecycle` on single-doc and batch decrypt paths so reads always expose a valid lifecycle to callers. (`src/repositories/CaseRepository.js`).
- Controller: Added `enforceDocketLifecycleDefault` to harden responses and applied it to single-case (`GET /api/cases/:id`) and list responses so payloads returned to UI always include a valid lifecycle. (`src/controllers/case.controller.js`).
- UI: Updated UI normalization fallback to `WL` and extended canonical mapping for `WL/ACTIVE/WAITING/DONE` so UI components never fall back to legacy `CREATED`/empty strings. (`ui/src/utils/lifecycle.js`).

### Testing

- Ran `npm run lint` and it passed.
- Performed `node --check` on modified files (`src/domain/docketLifecycle.js`, `src/models/Case.model.js`, `src/repositories/CaseRepository.js`, `src/controllers/case.controller.js`, `ui/src/utils/lifecycle.js`) and checks passed.
- Executed an inline Node assertion script validating `normalizeLifecycle` and `deriveLifecycle` fallbacks (e.g., `normalizeLifecycle(null) === DocketLifecycle.WL`) and it passed.
- The lifecycle workflow unit test file (`tests/docketLifecycleWorkflow.test.js`) was exercised during development, failing early due to stricter behavior and then corrected; fixes were validated via the lint/`node --check` and inline assertions described above.

author: tmchow
body:
## Summary

Two OpenAPI parser improvements that address the same root cause: the parser silently discards information from individual operations that it should preserve. Both were P1 findings from the Cal.com Run 2 retro (#135).

## Per-endpoint version header routing

When a required header (e.g., `cal-api-version`) has different values across endpoint groups, the parser previously promoted the majority value globally and discarded the rest. This caused 404s on ~20% of endpoints for APIs like Cal.com (bookings: `2024-08-13`, event-types: `2024-06-14`).

Now `detectRequiredHeaders()` tracks per-path values when they differ. The global `RequiredHeader` uses the majority value as the default. Endpoints with different values get `HeaderOverrides` on the `Endpoint` struct. The client template supports `WithHeaders` variants for all HTTP methods, and the command template passes overrides when present.

**Affected:** ~10% of catalog APIs with per-resource versioning (Cal.com, Twilio, enterprise APIs).

## Auth inference tier 4

When `securitySchemes`, query-param inference, and description inference all fail, the parser now scans operations for required `Authorization` header parameters. If found on >30% of operations, it infers Bearer auth with `Inferred: true`.

Cal.com's spec has no `securitySchemes`, no auth-like query params, and a minimal description with no auth keywords — but every endpoint has a required `Authorization` header parameter. All three existing tiers missed it.

**Affected:** ~20% of specs without formal security sections (auto-generated specs, internal APIs, Postman exports).

## Test plan

- 1126 tests pass (6 new)
- `TestDetectRequiredHeaders/multi-version header tracks per-endpoint overrides` — verifies event-types get overrides, bookings don't
- `TestInferAuthHeaderParam` — 5 test cases: positive detection, below-threshold, optional params, explicit securitySchemes precedence
- `TestAuthTierPrecedence` — existing tests still pass (tier ordering preserved)
- New test fixtures: `testdata/openapi/multi-version-header.yaml`, `testdata/openapi/auth-header-param.yaml`

author: harmonicrain
body:
## Summary

- **Reorder user removal and broadcast in `RemoveRoomUser`** to prevent the departing user from receiving their own `UserRemoveComposer (2661)`, which causes the Nitro client to tear down its room session and stop sending follow-up packets on subsequent room entries.

## Root Cause

When entering a room for the second time, `PrepareRoom` calls `RemoveUserFromRoom` to clean up the old room. Inside `RemoveRoomUser`, the order was:

```
1. Remove from game map
2. _room.SendPacket(UserRemoveComposer)  // broadcasts to ALL users in _users
3. _users.TryRemove(...)                  // removes from user list
```

Since the departing user was still in `_users` at step 2, `_room.SendPacket` iterated over them and sent `UserRemoveComposer (2661)` to their own client.

**Nitro behavior:** When Nitro receives `UserRemove` for its own avatar, it fires `RSE_ENDED` / `REE_DISPOSED` and tears down the room engine. The subsequent `RoomReady (2031)` arrives to a dead session, so Nitro never sends `GetFurnitureAliases (3898)` or `GetRoomEntryData (2300)`. Result: only background and bubbles visible, no floorplan or avatar.

**Flash behavior:** Flash had a more resilient state machine that ignored self-removal during room transitions, so this ordering never mattered.

## Fix

Swap the order: remove from `_users` **before** broadcasting `UserRemoveComposer`. The departing user is no longer in the iteration list and doesn't receive the packet, while all other users in the room still do.

## File Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `RoomUserManager.cs` | Moved `_users.TryRemove()` before `_room.SendPacket(UserRemoveComposer)` in `RemoveRoomUser()` |

## Summary

Audited all 21 `@unchecked Sendable` conformances in the codebase and removed 8 that are unnecessary:

- **ClaudeBackend, OpenAIBackend, KoboldCppBackend**: redundant — `@unchecked Sendable` is already declared on the `SSECloudBackend` superclass and inherited by all final subclasses
- **SwiftDataPersistenceProvider, MockPersistenceProvider**: `@MainActor` isolation already satisfies `Sendable` without needing `@unchecked`
- **ConfiguringOpenAICloudBackend, ConfiguringClaudeCloudBackend** (E2E tests): `final class` with only `let` stored properties of `Sendable` types — the compiler can verify safety statically
- **OrderCapturingTask** (UI tests): `final class` with only `let` stored properties (`Int` and `ActorBox`) — replaced `@unchecked Sendable` with `Sendable`

The remaining 13 `@unchecked Sendable` conformances are legitimate:
- **SSECloudBackend**: `open class` with NSLock-guarded mutable state (can't be verified statically for non-final classes)
- **OllamaBackend, FoundationBackend, SlowMockBackend**: NSLock-guarded mutable state
- **MLXBackend, LlamaBackend**: C interop wrappers with non-Sendable foreign types
- **MemoryPressureHandler, SettingsService**: `@Observable` with GCD/UserDefaults internals
- **ExtractiveCompressor, AnchoredCompressor**: mutable configuration properties
- **MockURLProtocol.StubbedResponse**: enum with `Error` associated value (Error is not Sendable)

author: dschramm99
body:
### 💡 What
This optimization implements two major performance improvements:
1. **Parallel Ticker Analysis**: Replaces the sequential for-loop in `app.py` with a `ThreadPoolExecutor` (max_workers=5) to analyze multiple tickers concurrently.
2. **Optimized Metadata Retrieval**: Replaces the slow `yf.Ticker(ticker).info` calls with a direct query to the Yahoo Finance search API in a centralized, cached function (`get_company_name`).

### 🎯 Why
- Sequential scanning of large indices (like S&P 500 or DAX) was a significant bottleneck, taking several minutes.
- `yf.Ticker.info` fetches a large JSON payload and is notoriously slow, adding 1-2 seconds per ticker just for the company name.

### 📊 Impact
- **Index Scans**: Expected speedup of ~3.7x to 5.5x for index analysis.
- **Metadata**: Retrieval of company names for the Top 5 results is now near-instant (cached) or ~10x faster (API vs full scrape).

### 🔬 Measurement
- The UI now displays the total duration of the signal generation process (e.g., "Fertig ✅ (Dauer: 12.4s)"). Users can compare this to previous manual timing.
- Metadata retrieval can be verified by the lack of "hanging" when the Top 5 table is first displayed.

### ♿ Accessibility & Safety
- Streamlit script context is explicitly passed to worker threads using `get_script_run_ctx` and `add_script_run_ctx` to ensure `@st.cache_data` and other session features continue to function correctly.
- Added 10s timeouts to all new network requests to prevent application hangs.

body:
## Promotion: develop -> main

> **Merge with "Create a merge commit".** This maintains the ancestry link between
> develop and main, preventing divergence on future promotions.

### Pre-merge checklist

- [ ] CI passes on develop
- [ ] Dev Docker images smoke-tested (`ghcr.io/.../glycemicgpt-*:dev`)
- [ ] Dev APK tested on device (from `dev-latest` release)
- [ ] No known regressions

### Notable changes since last promotion

<!-- List significant changes included in this promotion -->

-

### Versioning

Commit types in this promotion determine the version bump:

| Type | Bump | Example |
|------|------|---------|
| `fix:` | PATCH (0.3.0 -> 0.3.1) | Bug fix, CI fix (`fix(ci): ...`) |
| `feat:` | MINOR (0.3.0 -> 0.4.0) | New user-facing feature |
| `feat!:` / `BREAKING CHANGE:` | MINOR (while pre-1.0; MAJOR after 1.0) | Breaking API change |
| `chore:`, `ci:`, `docs:`, etc. | Fallback PATCH | Non-user-facing (auto patch) |

If all commits are non-releasable types (`chore:`, `ci:`, `docs:`, `test:`, `style:`, `build:`),
the release workflow automatically creates a patch release. Every promotion produces a versioned
release -- no manual intervention required.

### Post-merge steps

1. Release-please analyzes commits and either:
   - Creates a version bump PR (if `feat:`/`fix:` commits exist) -- glycemicgpt-merge auto-merges it
   - Does nothing (if only `chore:`/`ci:`/`docs:` commits) -- the fallback job creates a patch release automatically
2. Verify stable container images are published with new version tag
3. Verify signed release APK is uploaded to the GitHub release
4. Version sync happens automatically -- the `sync-main-to-develop` workflow
   cherry-picks the version bump back to develop via PR. Verify it completed
   in the [Actions tab](../../actions/workflows/sync-main-to-develop.yml).

author: clovenbradshaw-ctrl
body:
## Summary
Implement Phase 2 of progressive loading to enable incremental rendering of the card table as data streams in from IndexedDB. The card encoder now yields prototype overview first (<50ms), then card batches per chunk, allowing the UI to display results before all data is loaded.

## Key Changes

- **New async generator `loadChunks()`**: Yields batches in two phases:
  - Phase A: Prototype registry only (for quick overview)
  - Phase B: Card batches from each chunk (one per iteration)

- **New `buildCardBufferProgressive()` function**: Consumes `loadChunks()` with optional `onProgress` callback for incremental updates. Deduplicates cards by targetHash (latest temporal sequence wins) as chunks arrive.

- **New types**:
  - `LoadBatch`: Represents a yielded batch with phase, cards, registry, and chunk metadata
  - `CardBufferProgress`: Progress event emitted to callbacks with stage, buffer, entity count, and chunk info

- **Updated `initCardEncoder()`**: Now accepts optional `onProgress` callback and uses `buildCardBufferProgressive()` internally. Maintains backward compatibility (callback is optional).

- **Refactored `buildCardBuffer()`**: Now uses `loadChunks()` generator internally for consistency.

## Implementation Details

- The prototype phase fires first with `entityCount: 0` (no cards loaded yet), allowing the table view to render headers and metadata before chunks arrive
- Entity count increases monotonically across chunk callbacks, enabling progress indicators
- Deduplication logic preserves latest temporal sequence per targetHash across all chunks
- Registry is captured from the overview phase and used throughout initialization
- All changes are backward compatible; existing code calling `initCardEncoder()` without a callback continues to work

author: rjayasin
body:
## Summary
Fixes two bugs in `build_chunks()`:

**Bug 1 — First chunk could exceed the limit**
The `current != header` guard prevented a split on the first game line, so `header + "\n" + game_line_1` was always appended unconditionally regardless of length.

**Bug 2 — Labels pushed chunks over the limit**
Multi-part labels (`(1/3) `, `(2/3) `, etc.) were appended *after* chunking, meaning any chunk that was already at or near 140 chars would silently exceed the limit once labeled.

## Fix
- Introduce `_LABEL_OVERHEAD = 8` and subtract it from the limit upfront (`limit = SMS_CHUNK_LIMIT - _LABEL_OVERHEAD`), guaranteeing every chunk fits within 140 chars after labeling
- Remove the `current != header` special case — the limit now applies uniformly from the first line

author: sapiderman
body:
# PR

  This PR improves the user registration, improve robustness of the backend processing agent. It introduces a more resilient  architecture for email-based subscriptions, a new type-safe server action for web registrations, and polished UI components.

## Agent Architecture & Resilience
   * Decoupled Logic: Refactored the user-registration agent, moving core business logic to run.ts to improve testability.
   * Parallel Processing: Implemented concurrent message processing (limit: 5) for faster throughput of Outlook inbox items.
   * Robust Retries: Integrated withRetry with exponential backoff for all external service calls (Outlook Graph API, MediaPulse Data API, and Resend).
   * Rate Limiting: Added a per-email rate limiter (5 attempts/hour) to the agent to mitigate potential abuse from the inbox side.
   * Watermark Management: Improved tracking of receivedDateTime to ensure reliable idempotent processing across agent runs.

## New Registration Server Action
   * Type-Safe API: Introduced a new registration handler using route-action-gen and Zod for strict input validation.
   * Atomic Transactions: Leveraged Prisma transactions to ensure users and their ticker subscriptions are created or updated atomically.
   * Normalization: Automated ticker symbol normalization (trimming/casing) to prevent duplicate records.

## Enhanced UI/UX
   * Improved Form: Updated the RegistrationForm with a searchable ticker dropdown, real-time filtering, and better keyboard accessibility.
   * State Management: Integrated the useServerFunction hook for clean handling of loading, success, and error states.
   * Interactive Feedback: Added toast notifications and a dedicated "Subscription Confirmed" view upon successful registration.

## Email System Improvements
   * React Templates: Created new, brand-consistent email templates for registration-confirmation and invalid-ticker notifications using
     @workspace/email-templates.
   * Personalization: Templates now support dynamic ticker symbols and user-specific details.

## Testing & Quality
   * Expanded Coverage: Added comprehensive unit tests for the agent runner, server actions, and UI components, including edge cases for invalid inputs and
     rate limits.
   * Tooling: Updated package.json and tsconfig.json across packages to align with workspace standards.
   
   ## Checklist (`.cursor` rules)

- [x] I ran `pnpm code-quality` locally and it passed.
- [x] I ran `pnpm cursor:review -- --base origin/main --head HEAD` (or equivalent SHAs) and fixed any issues.
- [x] **Reuse before create:** I searched for existing components/utilities and reused or extended them instead of duplicating patterns.
- [x] **Route actions / handlers:** If I added or changed `route.*.config.ts` files, I followed the route-action-gen workflow (config + generator + tests).

body:
Implements staged expansion PR3: comprehensive, non-invasive SSL/TLS posture analysis integrated into the existing scan/report pipeline.

## New: `plugins/tls_inspector.py`

- **`TLSInspector`** — bounded handshake-based inspection with configurable timeout/retries; three-phase: primary handshake (`CERT_NONE`), trust verification (system CA), legacy protocol probes
- **`TLSResult` / `TLSCertInfo`** — structured result dataclasses with `to_dict()` (JSON-ready) and `to_findings()` (pipeline-compatible finding dicts with severity/status/evidence)
- **`is_tls_port()`** — port eligibility by known port set + service name keyword
- Enhanced cert parsing via `cryptography` when available (sig algo, key size, SANs); graceful stdlib fallback

**Checks performed:**

| Category | Details |
|---|---|
| Protocol | Negotiated version; legacy TLS 1.0/1.1 acceptance probe |
| Cipher | NULL (CRITICAL), RC4/EXPORT/anon (HIGH), 3DES (MEDIUM), no forward secrecy (MEDIUM) |
| Certificate | Expired/expiring, not-yet-valid, self-signed, untrusted chain, hostname/SAN mismatch |
| Key/Sig | RSA < 2048-bit, EC/DSA < 224-bit, SHA-1 (HIGH), MD5 (CRITICAL) |

## Pipeline integration (`vultron.py`)

- **Phase 1c** runs after TCP scan; findings staged in `_tls_staged_findings` and merged into `results['vulnerabilities']` after Phase 2 initialises the list (avoids overwrite bug)
- `tls_scan: {}` key always present in results; populated with per-port `TLSResult.to_dict()` output
- TLS findings carry `"category": "tls"` and flow through existing severity counters unchanged
- `--no-tls-inspect` / `--tls-timeout` / `--tls-retries` CLI flags; backward-compatible (UDP-only and `--no-tls-inspect` modes produce identical output to v4.1)
- HTML report extended with TLS inspection table; version bumped to 5.0.0

## Tests

92 new tests (333 total) covering: cert date parsing, hostname/wildcard matching, cipher/protocol severity classification, expiry windows, self-signed/untrusted/key/sig findings, `is_tls_port`, forward secrecy detection, graceful failure/retry, CLI flag parsing, pipeline integration (findings merge, `--no-tls-inspect` bypass, JSON output).

### 2) Certificate analysis
- Add checks for certificate quality and validity signals, including:
  - expiration / not-yet-valid windows
  - hostname/SAN matching (when hostname context exists)
  - self-signed / untrusted chain indicators
  - weak signature/hash algorithms (e.g., SHA-1/MD5 where applicable)
  - key size weaknesses (e.g., RSA too small, etc.)
- Record evidence and severity/priority consistent with repo schemas.

### 3) Protocol/cipher posture checks
- Add policy checks for insecure protocol/cipher posture, e.g.:
  - deprecated/legacy protocol support (SSLv2/SSLv3/TLS1.0/TLS1.1)
  - weak ciphers (NULL/EXPORT/RC4/3DES etc., as detectable)
  - forward secrecy presence indicator where inferable
- Keep checks non-invasive and based on bounded handshake attempts.

### 4) Optional HTTP-over-TLS metadata
- If service appears to be HTTPS, optionally capture minimal safe metadata useful for reporting (e.g., cert subject/issuer, HSTS header if already part of existing HTTP flow).
- Do not add exploit or intrusive web testing in this PR.

### 5) CLI integration
- Add/adjust CLI flags for TLS inspection controls in professional style, e.g.:
  - enable/disable TLS deep inspection
  - TLS timeout/retries
  - optional strictness/profile selection if architecture supports
- Ensure `-h` text reflects actual defaults and behavior.

### 6) Pipeline integration
- Run TLS inspection for relevant targets/ports discovered by TCP/UDP workflows as appropriate.
- Integrate findings into unified result model with clear category/tagging.
- Preserve existing scan behavior when TLS inspection disabled.

### 7) Reporting updates
- Extend JSON/HTML reports with a dedicated TLS section per host/service where applicable.
- Include concise risk summaries and evidence fields.
- Ensure no sensitive credential leakage in report paths.

### 8) Tests
Add/update tests for:
- certificate parsing and date validation
- protocol/cipher classification logic
- hostname match behavior (when hostname known)
- CLI parsing for TLS options
- pipeline/report integration for TLS findings
- graceful handling of handshake failures/timeouts

### 9) Documentation
- Update README with TLS inspection usage examples and caveats.
- Keep authorized-use and defensive language.
- Clarify this is posture analysis, not exploitation.

## Constraints
- Do not implement web-app vulnerability scanning here (reserved for later phase).
- Keep module boundaries clean for future expansion.
- Maintain backward compatibility for existing scan modes.

## Deliverable
- Single PR implementing SSL/TLS deep inspection with integrated findings, tests, and docs.

body:
`comingSoon: true` products always rendered `coming-soon.svg`, silently ignoring any assigned `image` field. The three Yu Gi Oh Exclusive Trading Card variants each had real images set but were never displayed.

## Change

Inverted the `bannerContent` priority in `payment.js` — check for a product image first, fall back to `coming-soon.svg` only for coming-soon products with no image:

```js
// Before
product.comingSoon ? <coming-soon.svg> : product.image ? <actual image> : <emoji>

// After
product.image ? <actual image> : product.comingSoon ? <coming-soon.svg> : <emoji>
```

This preserves the "Coming Soon" footer/button behavior while allowing the actual product photo to appear in the card banner.

author: jeremymcs
body:
## TL;DR

**What:** Coerce plain-string values to arrays for simple array fields in `gsd_complete_slice` tool schema and execute function.
**Why:** LLMs sometimes pass `provides` (and similar fields) as a string instead of `["string"]`, causing TypeBox validation to reject the call before coercion can run.
**How:** Accept `Union([Array(String), String])` in the schema for 8 simple array fields and add `wrapArray()` coercion in the execute function.

## What

Two files changed in `src/resources/extensions/gsd/`:
- `bootstrap/db-tools.ts` — schema + coercion logic for the `gsd_slice_complete` tool
- `tests/complete-slice-string-coercion.test.ts` — regression tests for `wrapArray` coercion

## Why

When the LLM generates `"provides": "Validated Tech UI flows..."` instead of `["Validated Tech UI flows..."]`, TypeBox schema validation fails with `provides: must be array` **before** the execute function runs. This causes "Structured argument generation failed — pausing auto-mode", blocking autonomous execution.

The complex object-array fields (`filesModified`, `requirementsAdvanced`, etc.) already had `Type.Union` fallbacks from #3541, but the 8 simple string-array fields (`provides`, `keyFiles`, `keyDecisions`, `patternsEstablished`, `observabilitySurfaces`, `requirementsSurfaced`, `drillDownPaths`, `affects`) did not.

Closes #3585

## How

1. Changed schema for all 8 simple array fields from `Type.Array(Type.String())` to `Type.Union([Type.Array(Type.String()), Type.String()])` so validation passes either way
2. Added `wrapArray()` helper that normalizes `null`/`undefined` → `[]` and `string` → `[string]`
3. Applied `wrapArray()` to all 13 array fields (8 simple + 5 complex), replacing the previous `?? []` pattern

### Change type

- [x] `fix` — Bug fix

### AI disclosure

This PR was AI-assisted.

### Test plan

- [x] All 15 coercion tests pass (5 new `wrapArray` unit tests + 10 existing)
- [x] Build succeeds
- [ ] Verify complete-slice no longer fails when LLM passes `provides` as a string

author: railway-app[bot]
body:
## Problem

The Spring Boot app crashes on startup with `java.net.UnknownHostException: postgres:AFELmJFzOBJtAdOAKNhSBqpGCQawkKDW@autorack.proxy.rlwy.net` because `application.yml` sets both `url: ${DATABASE_URL}` and separate `username`/`password` fields. When Spring's datasource builder receives a full connection URL alongside explicit credentials, it malforms the JDBC connection attempt, treating the credential-embedded URL as a raw hostname.

## Solution

Removed the `username: ${PGUSER}` and `password: ${PGPASSWORD}` lines from the datasource configuration in `server/src/main/resources/application.yml`. Railway's `DATABASE_URL` is already a complete connection string containing the credentials, host, port, and database name, so Spring can parse it correctly on its own without the conflicting individual credential fields.

### Changes
- **Modified** `server/src/main/resources/application.yml`

author: octo-patch
body:
Fixes #2441

## Problem

`_format_table` in `.github/scripts/aggregate_evals.py` uses Python's `or` operator to fall back to `\"n/a\"` for optional metrics:

```python
r.get("solve_rate") or "n/a",
r.get("step_ratio") or "n/a",
r.get("tool_call_ratio") or "n/a",
```

Since `0.0` is falsy in Python, this incorrectly displays `0.0` values as `\"n/a\"` in the evals summary table — making models with a zero solve/step/tool-call rate look like they didn't report those metrics at all.

## Solution

Replace the falsy checks with explicit `None` checks:

```python
"n/a" if r.get("solve_rate") is None else r.get("solve_rate"),
"n/a" if r.get("step_ratio") is None else r.get("step_ratio"),
"n/a" if r.get("tool_call_ratio") is None else r.get("tool_call_ratio"),
```

This correctly shows `0.0` for models that scored zero, while still showing `n/a` when the metric is absent (i.e., `None`).

## Testing

Verified locally with a simple script:
- `solve_rate=0.0` → now correctly shows `0.0` (was `n/a`)
- `solve_rate=None` → still correctly shows `n/a`
- `solve_rate=0.5` → still correctly shows `0.5`

body:
### Motivation

- Avoid an infinite redirect loop when the backend redirects the OAuth callback to a different frontend origin by marking that the redirect already happened. 

### Description

- Add `Cookie` usage to set a short-lived `oauth_google_callback_redirected` cookie when redirecting to the frontend so a subsequent hop won't re-redirect. 
- Stop forwarding the legacy redirect flag by checking the new cookie before performing the origin redirect. 
- Centralize callback URL construction into a new private method `frontendCallbackUrl(string $frontendUrl, string $token, string $user): string`. 
- Clear the `oauth_google_callback_redirected` cookie when returning the inline bridge HTML that writes `auth_token` and `auth_user` to `localStorage`.

### Testing

- Added feature tests in `backend/tests/Feature/Auth/GoogleOAuthTest.php` covering the legacy-flag case and the one-hop redirect prevention, and ran the Google OAuth feature tests. 
- All assertions in the modified feature tests passed.

author: denniskempin
body: ## Summary Resolves **SRE-5**: `decode_bgmode` previously panicked for modes 4, 6, and 7 while `write_bgmode` already accepted them, causing crashes at render time. ## Changes - **Mode 4**: Decode BG1 (8bpp), BG2 (2bpp), BG3 (4bpp, opt) with the same front-to-back priority order as modes 3 and 5 per the wiki table in `decode_bgmode`. - **Mode 6**: Decode BG1 (4bpp) and BG3 (4bpp, opt) with the mode-2-style priority stack (no BG2). - **Mode 7**: Implement affine background sampling: 128×128 tilemap at VRAM word `$0000`, 8bpp character data at word `$4000+` (standard `LoadM7VRAM` layout), including per-tile flip and priority from the map attribute byte. Add PPU writes for `$211A` (M7SEL) and full 16-bit paired writes for M7C, M7D, M7X, M7Y; extend M7B to store the full matrix value while keeping the existing 8-bit multiply operand behavior for `$2134–$2136`. ## Testing - `cargo build -p sres_emulator` - `cargo test -p sres_emulator` (library tests pass; some integration tests fail in this environment for unrelated reasons—e.g. missing LFS snapshot data, APU golden mismatch) - `cargo clippy -p sres_emulator --no-deps` (no new warnings in touched code) ## Notes Mode 7 is a first-pass implementation (e.g. M7EXTBG, mosaic, and exact hardware edge cases are not covered). The primary goal of this PR is **no panic** and a plausible render path for games that select these modes. Linear Issue: [SRE-5](https://linear.app/sres/issue/SRE-5/ppu-background-modes-4-6-and-7-panic-at-render-time)

author: effortlesssteven
body:
🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
💡 Vulnerability: A potential SQL injection vector existed in `swarm/api/routes/db.py` due to using Python f-strings to dynamically interpolate table names into a SQL query `conn.execute(f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM {table}")` without sanitization. Table names cannot be parameterized.
🎯 Impact: While this might only be hit internally by the stats endpoint, an attacker who could somehow manipulate the `table` argument could execute arbitrary SQL queries against the DuckDB projection database, leading to data exfiltration or corruption.
🔧 Fix: Implemented an explicit allowlist validation `{"runs", "steps", "tool_calls", "file_changes", "events", "facts"}` within the `safe_count` function to strictly ensure only valid table names are interpolated.
✅ Verification: Ran `uv run pytest tests/test_db_projection.py tests/test_resilient_db.py` to ensure database stats functionality remains intact and the fix introduces no regressions.

author: thomasjiangcy
body:
## What was changed

Updated the CI jobs in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` that were pinned to Blacksmith Linux runners so they now execute on GitHub-hosted Linux runners, while preserving the previous Blacksmith runner values as commented lines for easy reversal. The `TS Static` workflow step was also adjusted to invoke `oxlint` directly with `--threads=1`, which avoids the `spawnSync pnpm ENOMEM` failure that appeared on `ubuntu-latest`.

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: commented out the `blacksmith-2vcpu-ubuntu-2404` `runs-on` lines for `static-ts`, `static-rust`, `knip`, `test-ts`, and `test-rust`
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: added `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` immediately under each commented Blacksmith line so those jobs use GitHub's default Linux runner
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: changed the `static-ts` lint command to call `oxlint` directly with `--threads=1` before the existing OpenAPI, docs, SQL, and typecheck steps

## How to review

Start with `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and inspect the five job headers around the `static-ts`, `static-rust`, `knip`, `test-ts`, and `test-rust` definitions. Confirm that each job keeps the old Blacksmith runner in a comment and now points at `ubuntu-latest`. Then check the `static-ts` lint step and verify it now calls `oxlint` directly with `--threads=1`, while preserving the rest of the static check sequence.

To validate locally, run:

- `pnpm format`
- `pnpm lint`
- `pnpm typecheck`
- `pnpm test`
- `pnpm run ci`

## What the implication was

These CI jobs will stop requesting Blacksmith-hosted Linux capacity and will instead run on GitHub-hosted Linux runners. Because the previous runner strings remain commented in place, reverting back to Blacksmith later is a small, explicit workflow edit instead of reconstructing the old values from history. The `static-ts` step now uses a single-threaded `oxlint` invocation on GitHub-hosted runners so the workflow keeps the same lint coverage without failing under the lower-memory runner profile.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Before[CI jobs] --> Blacksmith[blacksmith-2vcpu-ubuntu-2404]
  After[CI jobs] --> GitHub[ubuntu-latest]
  Blacksmith -. preserved as comments .-> Workflow[.github/workflows/ci.yml]
```

## Checks and tests performed

- `pnpm format`: checked repository formatting; expected no formatting drift after the workflow edit; implemented by running the repo formatter across the worktree
- `pnpm lint`: checked TS/Rust/docs/OpenAPI linting; expected the workflow-only change to leave lint clean; implemented by running the repo lint entrypoint
- `pnpm typecheck`: checked workspace and script type safety; expected no type regressions from the workflow edit; implemented by running the repo typecheck entrypoint
- `pnpm test`: checked the repository test entrypoint; expected existing tests to remain green because no application logic changed; implemented by running the repo test entrypoint
- `pnpm run ci`: checked the full local CI mirror; expected the branch to satisfy the same combined checks used before push; implemented by running the repo CI script end-to-end
- `nix develop --command bash -lc "pnpm format:check && pnpm exec oxlint --type-aware --deny-warnings --threads=1 apps packages tests && pnpm lint:openapi && pnpm lint:docs && pnpm lint:sql && pnpm typecheck:ts"`: checked the exact `TS Static` workflow command after the ENOMEM failure; expected the same lint coverage to pass with `oxlint` constrained to one thread; implemented by running the workflow shell command locally inside the Nix dev environment

#### 1. ChinaMarketplaceEngine (중국 마켓플레이스 엔진)
- 전체 중국 구매 프로세스 오케스트레이션: 상품검색 → 가격비교 → 셀러검증 → 주문생성 → 결제 → 배송추적
- `ChinaPurchaseOrder` 데이터클래스: 중국 구매 주문 (order_id, marketplace, product_url, quantity, status, agent, timestamps 등)
- `ChinaPurchaseStatus` Enum: `created` → `agent_assigned` → `searching` → `seller_verified` → `ordering` → `paid` → `shipped` → `warehouse_received` → `completed`

#### 2. TaobaoAgent (타오바오 에이전트)
- `TaobaoAgent`: 타오바오 자동 구매 에이전트 mock
- 상품 검색 (키워드/URL 기반)
- 상품 상세 정보 조회 (가격, 배송비, 셀러 정보, 재고, SKU 옵션)
- 셀러 신뢰도 평가 (판매량, 평점, 운영기간 기반)
- 주문 생성 (배송대행지 주소 자동 설정)
- 주문 상태 추적
- 가격 흥정/쿠폰 자동 적용 시뮬레이션

#### 3. Alibaba1688Agent (1688 에이전트)
- `Alibaba1688Agent`: 1688 B2B 자동 구매 에이전트 mock
- 상품 검색 (키워드/URL 기반)
- MOQ(최소주문수량) 체크 + 단가 구간별 가격 조회
- 공장 직거래 vs 도매상 구분
- 샘플 주문 지원
- 대량 주문 할인 자동 협상 시뮬레이션
- 품질 인증서 확인 (mock)

#### 4. ChinaAgentManager (구매대행 에이전트 관리)
- `PurchasingAgent` ABC: 구매대행 에이전트 인터페이스 (search, get_detail, verify_seller, place_order, track_order)
- `AgentManager`: 에이전트 등록/관리, 주문 배정, 성과 추적
- 에이전트별 전문 분야 매칭 (의류/전자/식품 등 카테고리)
- 에이전트 평가 시스템 (처리속도, 정확도, 응답률)

#### 5. RPAController (RPA 자동화 컨트롤러)
- `RPAController`: 브라우저 자동화 시뮬레이션 mock
- `RPATask` 데이터클래스: RPA 작업 (task_id, type, status, steps, result)
- `RPAStep` 데이터클래스: RPA 단계 (step_id, action, target, value, screenshot_url)
- RPA 작업 유형: `search_product`, `place_order`, `check_status`, `apply_coupon`
- RPA 실행 이력 관리
- RPA 실패 시 수동 전환 알림

#### 6. SellerVerificationService (셀러 검증)
- `SellerVerificationService`: 셀러 신뢰도 종합 평가
- `SellerProfile` 데이터클래스: 셀러 프로필 (seller_id, name, rating, sales_count, years_active, verification_status 등)
- `SellerScore` 데이터클래스: 종합 점수 (reliability, quality, shipping_speed, communication, overall)
- 블랙리스트 관리 (사기/불량 셀러)
- 화이트리스트 관리 (검증된 우수 셀러)

#### 7. ChinaPaymentService (중국 결제 서비스)
- `ChinaPaymentService`: 알리페이/위챗페이 결제 mock
- `AlipayProvider`: 알리페이 결제 mock
- `WechatPayProvider`: 위챗페이 결제 mock
- 환율 자동 적용 (CNY ↔ KRW)
- 결제 한도 관리
- 결제 내역/영수증 관리

body: ## Description ### Core changes - Adds the `/dashboard/expenses` flow and wires it into the dashboard navigation. - Introduces the expenses provider, use cases, and API repository/client to list, create, update, and delete expenses against the authenticated backend. - Adds the expenses UI for summary, empty state, paginated list, create/edit modal, delete confirmation, and catalog selectors for currency, type, and optional category. - Loads currencies, expense types, and expense categories from the API and caches catalogs to avoid unnecessary refetching between visits. - Extends the dashboard translations in English and Spanish for the new expenses experience. ### Schema changes - No database schema changes. - No contract-breaking API schema changes in this PR. - Adds `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` to the client environment defaults so the expenses flow can reach the API. ### Minor changes - Adds reusable UI components used by the expenses flow: `Badge`, `EmptyState`, `LoadingSpinner`, `Modal`, `SelectorField`, `ConfirmDialog`, and `CurrencyDisplay`. - Adds shared utilities for cache storage and date formatting, plus the workspace dependencies required by the new dashboard flow. - Adds automated coverage for the app route, dashboard feature, UI components, translations, and shared utilities touched by this work. ## Screenshots/Recordings ## How to Test 1. Set `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` to an environment where the expenses endpoints are available and start the client with `pnpm --filter @client/main web`. 2. Sign in and open `/dashboard/expenses` from the dashboard sidebar or directly in the browser. 3. Verify the page loads the current expenses, total count, and selector data for currencies, expense types, and categories without console or network errors. 4. Click `+ New expense`, create a record with a name, value, currency, and type, and confirm the modal closes and the new expense appears in the list. 5. Open an existing expense, update at least one field, and confirm the list refreshes with the latest values. 6. Delete an expense from the list, confirm the dialog, and verify the record is removed after the refresh. 7. If the account has enough records, scroll to the bottom and confirm more expenses load without duplicating the existing entries. ## Checklist - [x] The PR description includes clear instructions on how to test the implementation manually. ##### Added Tests? - [x] yes - [x] Verified that this PR is not creating duplicate use cases - [x] All edge cases described in the acceptance criteria are covered, and tests have clear and descriptive names - [ ] no, because they aren't needed - [ ] no, because I need help _Override these when needed._ ```sh ```

## Summary - Adds `rules_installer` adapter capability with `install-rules` / `check-rules` / `uninstall-rules` protocol subcommands, so each adapter binary owns how agent-native rule files are written - Claude Code adapter installs `.claude/rules/ox.md`; Droid adapter installs `.factory/rules/ox.md` — both with version-stamped content via agentx `RulesManager` - `ox init` now calls adapters to install rules; `ox doctor` detects missing/stale rules via adapter diagnostics; `ox uninstall` removes rules through adapters - `DiagnoseParams` gains a `Version` field so adapters can detect stale rules against the running ox version - Bumps agentx to v0.1.7 (adds generalized `BaseRulesManager` for 7 agents) and ox to v0.6.2 ## Architecture ```mermaid graph LR CLI["ox CLI
(init / doctor / uninstall)"] -->|adapter protocol| A1["ox-adapter-claude-code"] CLI -->|adapter protocol| A2["ox-adapter-droid"] A1 -->|library| AX["agentx RulesManager"] A2 -->|library| AX AX -->|writes| R1[".claude/rules/ox.md"] AX -->|writes| R2[".factory/rules/ox.md"] ``` ## Test plan - [ ] `go test ./pkg/adapterruntime/` — 4 new tests for rules subcommand dispatch - [ ] `go test ./cmd/ox-adapter-claude-code/` — 6 new tests (install, check, uninstall, idempotency, diagnose) - [ ] `go test ./cmd/ox-adapter-droid/` — 6 new tests (same matrix for `.factory/rules/`) - [ ] `make lint` — 0 issues - [ ] `ox init` in test repo creates `.claude/rules/ox.md` with agentx stamp - [ ] `ox doctor` detects missing/stale rules via adapter diagnostics - [ ] `ox uninstall` removes adapter-managed rule files Co-Authored-By: [SageOx](https://github.com/SageOx) ## Summary by CodeRabbit ## Release Notes – v0.6.2 * **New Features** * Added rule management capabilities (install, check, uninstall) through the adapter protocol * Implemented version-aware rule tracking for stale-rule detection during diagnostics * Adapters now advertise rules-installer capability * **Tests** * Added comprehensive end-to-end tests for rules lifecycle and diagnosis integration * **Chores** * Updated agentx dependency to v0.1.7 * Bumped version to 0.6.2

body:
## Summary

Adds Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, and .dockerignore so users can run SEO Machine in a container without manually installing Python dependencies.

## Changes

- `Dockerfile` - Python 3.12-slim base, installs system deps (gcc, libxml2) and Python packages from `data_sources/requirements.txt`
- `docker-compose.yml` - Single `seomachine` service with env_file pointing to `data_sources/config/.env` and volume mounts for all content directories (context, drafts, output, published, research, rewrites, topics, credentials, .claude)
- `.dockerignore` - Excludes .git, credentials, user content dirs, and cache files from the build context
- `README.md` - Added Docker Setup section after existing setup instructions
- `QUICK-START.md` - Added Docker Alternative subsection in Step 1

## Usage

```bash
# Configure credentials first
cp .env.example data_sources/config/.env
# Edit data_sources/config/.env with your API keys

# Build and run
docker-compose build
docker-compose run seomachine bash
```

Content directories are mounted as volumes so all work persists on the host.

## Simulated Demo

![Docker setup demo](https://files.catbox.moe/m5qx8d.gif)

Fixes #19

author: copilot
body:
Monolithic 1033-line `app.py` → modular architecture with live NHL API data, Monte Carlo simulations, position-specific player ratings, and league-wide projections for all 32 teams.

## Architecture

Decomposed into layered modules:

- **`config/`** — Team mappings (32 teams), logo URLs (NHL CDN), API endpoints, rating weights, stoplight thresholds
- **`providers/`** — `NHLApiProvider` with retry/backoff, `@st.cache_data` caching, health tracking per source; `DataHealth` for degraded-mode detection
- **`schemas/`** — Validators for standings, schedules, team games, playoff odds, projected records
- **`features/`** — `compute_momentum` (8-component composite → 0–100 + Hot/Steady/Slipping/Cold), `compute_player_ratings` (separate forward/defenseman/goalie formulas), `compute_team_features` (projected W-L-OTL with regression-to-mean blending)
- **`models/`** — `PlayoffModel` (odds from pace + GD + position + uncertainty), `project_seeds` (NHL division-top-3 + wildcard rules), `project_opponents` (1v8, 2v7, 3v6, 4v5 bracket)
- **`simulations/`** — Poisson-based MC game sim (10K runs, home/away splits, momentum adj), season sim (per-team remaining-schedule projection → conference playoff cutoff ranking)
- **`ui/`** — `charts.py` (Plotly figures), `components.py` (logo HTML, KPI cards, stoplight helpers), `styles.py` (CSS)
- **`utils/`** — `helpers.py` (flatten_dict, zscore, parse_mmss, etc.), `stoplight.py` (green/yellow/red styling for grades, momentum, odds, results)

## App (`app.py`)

Thin orchestration layer. 9 tabs:

| Tab | Content |
|-----|---------|
| Team Profile | Identity card, projected finish, trends, last 5 / next 5 |
| Playoff Race | Conference standings with projected seeds, opponents, MC odds |
| Team Comparison | Any two teams side-by-side with MC sim data |
| Next Game | Projected score, win %, OT %, goal distributions |
| Shot Maps | Offensive/defensive heat maps with zone summary |
| Player Ratings | Position-specific grades, TOI tracking, trend flags |
| Game Simulation | MC sim with forced home/away choice |
| Game Log | Schedule, team log, player log with stoplights |
| Data Health | Source status, warnings, degraded mode |

## Default behavior

Edmonton is the default focus. If MC sim projects elimination (`makePlayoffsPct < 1`), focus shifts to Western Conference race. Season state auto-detected: `regular_season` → `bracket_locked` → `active_playoff`.

## Tests

74 unit tests across `test_features.py`, `test_models.py`, `test_simulations.py`, `test_stoplight.py`:

```python
# Example: MC game sim validates probability coherence
def test_probabilities_sum_to_100(self):
    result = simulate_game("EDM", "CGY", standings, n_sims=1000)
    total = result["homeWinPct"] + result["awayWinPct"]
    assert abs(total - 100) < 1

# Example: stronger team gets higher playoff odds
def test_strong_team_higher_playoff_odds(self):
    results = simulate_season(standings, n_sims=500)
    assert results["COL"]["makePlayoffsPct"] >= results["CGY"]["makePlayoffsPct"]
```

author: buryitaway-boop
body:
## Problem

`speech_to_text` 7.3.0 fails to compile on macOS when using Swift Package Manager (SPM) instead of CocoaPods.

The `Package.swift` declares `.macOS("10.14")` but several types in `SpeechToTextPlugin.swift` (e.g. `SFTranscription`) require macOS 10.15+.

This causes Xcode to emit:
```
'SFTranscription' is only available in macOS 10.15 or newer
```

Related issues: #662, #649

## Fix

One-line change: bump `.macOS("10.14")` → `.macOS("10.15")` in `speech_to_text/darwin/speech_to_text/Package.swift`.

This aligns the SPM minimum deployment target with the actual API requirements of the plugin code.

body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #21146

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`tool.execute.after` fires for MCP tools before the output text is assembled from the raw `CallToolResult.content[]` array. Plugins receive the raw SDK result instead of the `{title, output, metadata}` shape declared in the `Hooks` type definition.

Any plugin that tries to transform `output.output` gets `undefined`, and the text assembly at L502-536 rebuilds the output from `result.content` independently of any hook mutations. The hook is effectively a no-op for MCP tool output transformation.

This moves the trigger call to after text assembly and truncation, passing an `assembled` object that matches the declared type contract. The return statement references the assembled object so plugin mutations are reflected in the final tool output.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Typecheck: all packages pass (the `npm-package-arg` error in `shared.ts` is pre-existing on dev)
- The change is limited to MCP tool execution in `prompt.ts`. Native tools (bash, read, etc.) are unaffected — they have their own hook paths
- Confirmed that the assembled object shape matches the `Hooks` type definition in `packages/plugin/src/index.ts`

N/A — no UI change.

- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

author: joelkoz
body:
## Summary
Parse raw websocket data before matching pending PUT responses by requestId.

## Problem
When a websocket client responds to a PUT request, the temporary listener in  receives raw  frames from Primus. The code was treating that raw payload as an already-parsed object and checking  directly.

For clients like SensESP that reply with JSON text such as:

 ```json
  {"requestId":"...","state":"COMPLETED","statusCode":200}
  ```

that meant the completion response was ignored, the request stayed PENDING, and Signal K timed it out after 60 seconds with a 504.

## Fix
  - accept unknown in the temporary websocket PUT listener
  - if the incoming payload is a string or buffer, JSON.parse(String(msg))
  - only then match requestId and call updateRequest()

## Verification

  Confirmed locally on a live v2.24.0 system with a SensESP device acting as a PUT target:

  - before the patch, every switch PUT timed out exactly 60 seconds later
  - after the patch, the server matched the completion payload and no 504 occurred

The device payload was:
```json
  {"requestId":"...","state":"COMPLETED","statusCode":200}
```

author: shubham-astro
body: ## Description - The tmp emptyDir volume mount on the git-sync container was gated behind `{{- if eq .Values.gitSyncRelay.repoFetchMode "webhook" }}`, meaning it was only mounted when using webhook fetch mode. Since Sanic now runs regardless of repoFetchMode, poll-mode deployments start Sanic without a writable /tmp, causing the SyncManager process to crash with `FileNotFoundError: No usable temporary directory found in ['/tmp', '/var/tmp', '/usr/tmp', '/']` and the pod to fail. - In git_daemon share mode, the git-daemon container crashes on startup with touch: cannot touch `'/git/.git/git-daemon-export-ok': Permission denied.` The git-repo-contents emptyDir is written by the git-sync container running as `uid=50000/gid=65533,` which creates `/git/.git/ ` with 755 permissions. The git-daemon container runs as a different UID and has no write access to that directory, causing the liveness probe (`touch /git/.git/git-daemon-export-ok`) to fail immediately and the container to crashloop. ## Related Issues https://linear.app/astronomer/issue/PLX-281/gitsync-deployments-are-not-turning-healthy ## Testing - Added unittests - I was able to stabilise the git-sync-relay pods: ## Merging Master, 1.17

author: pruebaics00-glitch
body:
💡 **What**: Refactored `PoiDAO` and `PoiResource` to construct the GeoJSON `FeatureCollection` directly inside PostgreSQL using `json_build_object` and `json_agg`, rather than iterating and using Jackson's `ObjectMapper` in memory on the Java side.

🎯 **Why**: Generating JSON in Java by instantiating maps/lists and parsing raw geometry strings with `ObjectMapper.readTree` adds significant CPU overhead and generates massive amounts of short-lived objects leading to high Garbage Collection pauses, especially for large geographic datasets. Offloading this directly to the database leverages PostGIS's highly optimized native C implementation for JSON creation, completely bypassing Java-side serialization.

📊 **Impact**: Reduces backend memory allocation and GC overhead drastically. Eliminates the `ObjectMapper` parsing loop entirely, returning a simple pre-computed String in an $O(1)$ backend operation.

🔬 **Measurement**: Verify by benchmarking the `/api/pois` endpoint with a large dataset using a load testing tool like `wrk` or `jmeter` to observe improved latencies, higher throughput, and reduced JVM heap usage. Tests pass properly locally.

author: copilot
body:
When a VPS is reinstalled, its SSH host fingerprint changes, causing `appleboy/ssh-action` to fail with a host-key mismatch until manually resolved.

## Changes

- **`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`** — adds `port`, `request_pty`, and `extra_args` to the `Deploy to VPS` step:

```yaml
port: 22
request_pty: true
# Skip host key verification so VPS reinstalls (which change the SSH
# fingerprint) don't break deployments. The connection is still
# authenticated via VPS_SSH_KEY. Update VPS_HOST_KEY secret if you
# want strict fingerprint pinning instead.
extra_args: "-o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null"
```

Authentication via `VPS_SSH_KEY` is unaffected — only fingerprint pinning is disabled. The `script:` block is unchanged.

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## Problem

When the VPS is reinstalled, its SSH host fingerprint changes. The current `deploy.yml` workflow using `appleboy/ssh-action@v1.0.3` fails because it sees a different fingerprint from the one previously trusted, breaking all deployments until someone manually intervenes.

## Solution

Add `StrictHostKeyChecking=no` and `UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null` via `extra_args` in the `appleboy/ssh-action` step in `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`. This makes the deployment workflow resilient to VPS reinstalls without requiring any manual secret updates.

The SSH connection remains secure — traffic is still encrypted and authenticated via the `VPS_SSH_KEY` private key. We are only skipping fingerprint pinning, which is acceptable for a CI/CD deployment workflow.

## Changes Required

**File: `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`**

Update the `Deploy to VPS` step to add:
```yaml
extra_args: "-o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null"
```

The full updated step should look like:
```yaml
      - name: Deploy to VPS
        uses: appleboy/ssh-action@v1.0.3
        with:
          host: ${{ secrets.VPS_HOST }}
          username: ${{ secrets.VPS_USER }}
          key: ${{ secrets.VPS_SSH_KEY }}
          port: 22
          request_pty: true
          extra_args: "-o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null"
          script: |
            set -euo pipefail
            cd ~/360-v2
            ... (rest of script unchanged)
```

Also add a comment above `extra_args` explaining why it's there, so future maintainers understand the intent:
```yaml
          # Skip host key verification so VPS reinstalls (which change the SSH
          # fingerprint) don't break deployments. The connection is still
          # authenticated via VPS_SSH_KEY. Update VPS_HOST_KEY secret if you
          # want strict fingerprint pinning instead.
          extra_args: "-o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null"
```

The `script:` block content must remain **completely unchanged**.

author: jingw6
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1502 — three gaps found during adversarial review of #1482:

- **Detect hook-blocked tool responses in semantic-retry** — `wrapToolCall` now detects `metadata.blockedByHook` on tool responses. Treats them as a deliberate no-op on retry state (no records, no budget, no pendingAction, no signal changes) since policy denials are permanent. Event-trace independently classifies them as `outcome="failure"`.
- **Surface preservation failures in enforce-budget** — `onBeforeDrop` callback errors are now captured as `preservationFailed`/`preservationError` fields on the result (fail-open) instead of being silently swallowed by empty catches.
- **Wire retrySignalReader through production runtime** — `createRuntime()` accepts `retrySignalReader` in `RuntimeConfig` and threads it into per-stream event-trace middleware, so retry annotations appear in real trajectories (not just golden recordings). Also threads `agentName`.

## Design decisions (from 8 rounds of Codex adversarial review)

- Hook-blocked path is a **full no-op** on semantic-retry state — no records appended (prevents retry numbering pollution), no budget consumed, no pendingAction or signal changes (preserves prior legitimate retry state)
- **Fail-open** for preservation — `preservationFailed` flag lets callers decide policy; blocking would stall the agent loop on flaky persistence
- `RetrySignalReader` is L0 (`@koi/core`) — no new L2 dependencies in runtime

## Test plan

- [x] 6 new semantic-retry tests: blockedByHook detection, signal preservation, budget unchanged, stale pendingAction preserved, normal/redacted passthrough
- [x] 3 new enforce-budget tests: sync throw, async reject, success (no flag)
- [x] 1 new create-runtime test: retrySignalReader accepted and threaded
- [x] `bun run typecheck` — all tasks pass
- [x] Biome lint clean (pre-commit hooks)
- [x] E2e: TUI boots and runs 2 turns; programmatic test verifies broker lifecycle

### [`v19.2.0`](https://redirect.github.com/facebook/react/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#1920-October-1st-2025)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/facebook/react/compare/v19.1.7...v19.2.0)

Below is a list of all new features, APIs, and bug fixes.

Read the [React 19.2 release post](https://react.dev/blog/2025/10/01/react-19-2) for more information.

##### New React Features

- [`<Activity>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity): A new API to hide and restore the UI and internal state of its children.
- [`useEffectEvent`](https://react.dev/reference/react/useEffectEvent) is a React Hook that lets you extract non-reactive logic into an [Effect Event](https://react.dev/learn/separating-events-from-effects#declaring-an-effect-event).
- [`cacheSignal`](https://react.dev/reference/react/cacheSignal) (for RSCs) lets your know when the `cache()` lifetime is over.
- [React Performance tracks](https://react.dev/reference/dev-tools/react-performance-tracks) appear on the Performance panel’s timeline in your browser developer tools

##### New React DOM Features

- Added resume APIs for partial pre-rendering with Web Streams:
  - [`resume`](https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/server/resume): to resume a prerender to a stream.
  - [`resumeAndPrerender`](https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/static/resumeAndPrerender): to resume a prerender to HTML.
- Added resume APIs for partial pre-rendering with Node Streams:
  - [`resumeToPipeableStream`](https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/server/resumeToPipeableStream): to resume a prerender to a stream.
  - [`resumeAndPrerenderToNodeStream`](https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/static/resumeAndPrerenderToNodeStream): to resume a prerender to HTML.
- Updated [`prerender`](https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/static/prerender) APIs to return a `postponed` state that can be passed to the `resume` APIs.

##### Notable changes

- React DOM now batches suspense boundary reveals, matching the behavior of client side rendering. This change is especially noticeable when animating the reveal of Suspense boundaries e.g. with the upcoming `<ViewTransition>` Component. React will batch as much reveals as possible before the first paint while trying to hit popular first-contentful paint metrics.
- Add Node Web Streams (`prerender`, `renderToReadableStream`) to server-side-rendering APIs for Node.js
- Use underscore instead of `:` IDs generated by useId

author: octo-patch
body:
Fixes #1473

## Problem

The default `api_version` in `DocumentIntelligenceConverter` was hardcoded to `"2024-07-31-preview"`, which is an outdated preview version that is **not compatible** with Azure AI Foundry Document Intelligence service endpoints.

The Azure AI Document Intelligence SDK's own default is `"2024-11-30"`, but markitdown was overriding it with the older preview version. This caused failures when users tried to use markitdown with Azure AI Foundry endpoints without explicitly specifying `docintel_api_version`.

## Solution

Update the default `api_version` from `"2024-07-31-preview"` to `"2024-11-30"` (the GA stable version). This version is compatible with both classic Azure Document Intelligence endpoints and Azure AI Foundry service endpoints.

## Testing

The change is a one-line default value update. Users who need the older preview version can still pass `docintel_api_version="2024-07-31-preview"` explicitly. No behavioral changes for users who already specify their api_version.

author: createkr
body:
# Fix: persist airdrop dedup state so duplicate claims survive restart

## Problem

Duplicate-claim prevention in `cross-chain-airdrop` was purely in-memory (`HashSet` inside `VerificationPipeline`). After any process restart — including every CLI invocation — all dedup state was lost, allowing the same GitHub account or wallet to claim again.

## Solution

Introduced a `ClaimStore` trait with two implementations:

| Implementation | Persistence | Use case |
|---|---|---|
| `InMemoryClaimStore` | None (volatile) | Backward compat, testing |
| `SqliteClaimStore` | SQLite file | Production, CLI |

The pipeline is now generic over `S: ClaimStore`. `VerificationPipeline::new()` still defaults to `InMemoryClaimStore` (no breaking change). A new `with_store()` constructor accepts any implementation.

The CLI uses `SqliteClaimStore` by default when built with `--features sqlite-store`, writing to `airdrop_claims.sqlite` in the working directory.

## Key changes

- **`src/claim_store.rs`** (new) — `ClaimStore` trait, `InMemoryClaimStore`, `SqliteClaimStore` (feature-gated)
- **`src/pipeline.rs`** — generic over `S: ClaimStore`; `new()` delegates to `with_store(..., InMemoryClaimStore::new())`
- **`src/bin/airdrop_cli.rs`** — conditional compilation: `SqliteClaimStore` when feature enabled, `InMemoryClaimStore` otherwise
- **`Cargo.toml`** — optional `rusqlite` dep + `sqlite-store` feature

## Tests

- 3 new `InMemoryClaimStore` tests
- 3 new `SqliteClaimStore` tests (including `test_sqlite_survives_reopen` which proves state persists across DB close/reopen)
- All 43 tests pass with `--features sqlite-store`
- All 40 tests pass without the feature

## Compatibility

- No breaking changes — `VerificationPipeline::new()` signature unchanged
- `sqlite-store` feature is opt-in; zero new dependencies for existing users
- All existing tests pass without modification

body:
### Security Enhancements in `internal/config`

This PR strengthens the security of the configuration resolution process through two primary improvements:

1.  **Expanded Input Validation**: The `ResolveWithFS` function now applies strict character validation (blocking ASCII control characters) to a comprehensive set of configuration fields. This includes not just images and users, but also runtime names, socket paths, logging formats, and all elements within environment variables, port mappings, and DNS settings. This prevents various injection attacks and ensures log integrity.
2.  **Broader Sensitive Data Masking**: The environment variable masking logic has been enhanced with additional keywords frequently associated with sensitive data: `CERT`, `PEM`, `PRIVATE`, `CREDENTIALS`, and `PASSPHRASE`. This reduces the risk of accidental exposure of certificates, private keys, and other credentials in dry-run or debug outputs.

**Testing performed:**
- Added new test cases to `TestMaskSensitiveEnv` in `internal/config/masking_test.go` for the newly added keywords.
- Added `TestUnit_Config_ResolveWithFS_SecurityValidation` in `internal/config/path_security_test.go` to verify that character validation correctly catches malicious input in both scalar and slice configuration fields.
- Verified that all existing tests in `internal/config` continue to pass.

- Add \`databaseClient.fetchImportedIssueByIdentifier\` for branch-name-to-issue lookup
- Add \`WorktreeConfig.extractIssueIdentifier(fromBranchName:)\` with anchored regex (avoids false positives like \`fix-47\`)
- Three new \`WorktreeFeature\` actions: \`syncRepo\`, \`syncAllRepos\`, \`repoSynced\`
- Hook into \`worktreesLoaded\` (background re-sync on every launch) and \`repoAdded(.success)\` (initial discovery)

- Add "Refresh worktrees" menu item to repo overflow menu for manual sync
- Convert string-based cancellation IDs to a typed \`CancelID\` enum per TCA R9
- All sync work happens off the main thread in \`Effect.run\` blocks

author: parsofish
body:
## Why

The `configure.ps1` script declares service URLs as parameters but hardcoded port numbers (7878 for Radarr, 8989 for Sonarr) directly in function bodies when calling Overseerr APIs and composing Prowlarr configuration payloads. This creates three problems:

1. **Duplication**: Ports are defined in multiple places (param defaults, API payloads, URL strings), making updates fragile and error-prone.
2. **Non-overridable**: There's no way to change ports except by modifying the script — environment-based configuration isn't supported.
3. **Configuration brittleness**: The `Wait-ForService` function has hardcoded retry logic (30 attempts, 2-second sleeps) that can't be tuned without code changes.

When service ports are customized (common in CI/CD or non-standard deployments), the script would still configure them with hardcoded defaults, breaking service discovery.

## Approach

Introduced a two-part refactor:

**Part 1: Port Parameterisation**
- Added `$RadarrPort` and `$SonarrPort` script parameters that:
  - Read from `$env:RADARR_PORT` / `$env:SONARR_PORT` when set
  - Fall back to defaults (7878 / 8989) when environment variables are absent
  - Are used consistently throughout: URL parameter defaults, Prowlarr API payloads, and Overseerr API configurations

**Part 2: Configurable Retry Logic**
- Added `$SleepSeconds` parameter to `Wait-ForService` that reads from `$env:WAIT_RETRY_SECS` (default 2)
- Updated `$MaxAttempts` parameter to read from `$env:WAIT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (default 30)
- Replaced hardcoded `Start-Sleep -Seconds 2` with the parameter

This approach:
- Preserves backwards compatibility (defaults match original hardcoded values)
- Centralizes port configuration in a single location (param block)
- Allows dynamic configuration via environment variables
- Eliminates port literals from function bodies

## Testing

**Unit Tests**: Created 28 tests in `Test-PortParameterisation.Tests.ps1` covering:
- Parameter declarations (`$RadarrPort` / `$SonarrPort` / `$MaxAttempts` / `$SleepSeconds` exist with correct defaults)
- No port literals (7878/8989) outside param block
- API payloads reference variables, not literals (covers all 4 functions: Add-RadarrToOverseerr, Add-SonarrToOverseerr, Add-RadarrToProwlarr, Add-SonarrToProwlarr)
- Wait-ForService retry parameters are configurable

These tests enforce the acceptance criteria and prevent regressions.

**Integration Tests**: Run `./dev-testing/test.ps1 -Quick` to validate syntax and general functionality (existing test suite, no regressions).

## Notes

- All hardcoded port literals (7878, 8989) now appear only in the param block as defaults — never in function bodies.
- The refactor is a pure enhancement with zero breaking changes: existing scripts continue to work unchanged.
- Both PowerShell and Bash parity is maintained (this change is PowerShell-specific, but equivalent logic exists in `configure.sh`).
- Follow-up: Consider applying the same pattern to `configure.sh` for feature parity.

body:
Builds a production-ready FlipClock application on top of the existing Flutter clean architecture scaffold, adding 6 screens, a realistic flip-card animation engine, a fully persisted theme system, and GoRouter-based tab navigation.

## Core flip animation (`lib/widgets/`)
- **`FlipCard`** — Split-flap animation via `Matrix4.rotateX` + perspective. Two-phase: old bottom half folds to π/2, new bottom half unfolds from π/2. Shadow overlay adds depth mid-flip.
- **`DigitPair`** — Two `FlipCard` instances for a two-digit field (hours, minutes, seconds)
- **`SeparatorWidget`** — Pulsing `:` colon using `AnimationController.repeat(reverse: true)`
- **`FlipClockDisplay`** — Composites all above; reads all visual config from `settingsProvider`

```dart
// Each digit flips independently only when its value changes
void didUpdateWidget(FlipCard oldWidget) {
  if (oldWidget.digit != widget.digit) {
    _nextDigit = widget.digit;
    _controller.forward(from: 0).then((_) {
      setState(() => _currentDigit = _nextDigit);
      _controller.reset();
    });
  }
}
```

## Theme system
- **`FlipClockTheme`** — Immutable data class (cardColor, cardTextColor, backgroundColor, separatorColor, accentColor, cardBorderRadius, flipDurationMs, glowEnabled, glowColor, fontFamily, BackgroundStyle). JSON-serializable for SharedPreferences persistence.
- **`SettingsNotifier`** / **`ClockFormatNotifier`** — SharedPreferences-backed `StateNotifier`s for all flip-clock and clock-format settings.
- Default dark preset: `#0D0D0D` background, `#E8A020` amber cards, `#FFF8E7` cream text.

## Feature screens & providers
| Screen | Key implementation detail |
|---|---|
| **Clock** | `StreamProvider<DateTime>` emitting every second; 12/24h toggle persisted |
| **Stopwatch** | 30ms `Timer.periodic`; lap tracking with best/worst index recomputed on each lap |
| **Timer** | `ListWheelScrollView` drum-roll pickers; red flash overlay on completion |
| **Pomodoro** | Phase state machine (work → shortBreak → longBreak); `CustomPainter` arc progress ring |
| **Focus** | Full-screen immersive; 4s inhale/hold/exhale breathing animation; rotating motivational quotes |
| **Settings** | Color swatches, flip-speed slider, border-radius slider, glow toggle, Pomodoro duration sliders |

## Navigation
- `StatefulShellRoute.indexedStack` for 5 tabs (Clock | Stopwatch | Timer | Pomodoro | Focus) — keeps all branch state alive.
- `/settings` as a root-level `GoRoute` above the shell (no bottom nav).
- `AuthGuard` updated to redirect authenticated users to `/clock`.

## Dependencies added to `pubspec.yaml`
`hooks_riverpod`, `flutter_hooks`, `audioplayers`, `vibration`, `google_fonts`, `wakelock_plus`, `flutter_local_notifications`, `intl`
