author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

Adds the **inventory-service** — a standalone .NET 8 Web API microservice extracted from the OrderManager monolith. This is the first service in a monorepo layout under `services/inventory-service/`, with accompanying IaC and CI/CD.

**Service** (`services/inventory-service/`):
- .NET 8 Web API with CRUD endpoints plus `check-stock` / `deduct-stock` for monolith integration
- Angular 17 standalone frontend (inventory list with low-stock filtering and inline restock)
- EF Core with SQLite, seed data for 5 products
- Health check at `/health` (wired to K8s probes)
- 9 xUnit unit tests covering all `InventoryItemService` methods

**IaC**:
- Multi-stage Dockerfile (Node → .NET SDK → Alpine runtime)
- Helm chart with NetworkPolicy (default-deny + ingress-nginx/monitoring allow), ServiceMonitor, HPA, liveness/readiness probes
- ArgoCD Application manifests for `decomposition-dev` and `decomposition-staging` namespaces

**CI/CD** (`.github/workflows/inventory-service-ci.yaml`):
- Path-scoped triggers (`services/inventory-service/**`)
- Build → test → push to ECR (on main only)

Companion monolith refactoring PR: [app_dotnet-angular-monolith#210](https://github.com/Cognition-Partner-Workshops/app_dotnet-angular-monolith/pull/210) — replaces direct DB inventory access with HTTP calls to this service. Both PRs should be reviewed together.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **No concurrency control on stock mutations** — `DeductStockAsync` and `RestockAsync` use plain `SaveChangesAsync` with no optimistic concurrency token or row-level lock. Concurrent requests can race past `CheckStockAsync` and cause over-deduction. Verify this is acceptable for the workshop scope or add a concurrency token on `InventoryItem`.
- [ ] **SQLite is not production-viable** — The service uses a local `inventory.db` file. Pods will lose data on restart and SQLite doesn't handle concurrent writes well. The Helm chart does not mount a PersistentVolume. Confirm this is intentional (workshop/demo only) or swap to PostgreSQL before staging deployment.
- [ ] **CORS allows any origin** — `Program.cs` sets `AllowAnyOrigin().AllowAnyMethod().AllowAnyHeader()`. Fine for local dev, but the same binary deploys to staging via ArgoCD. Consider restricting origins via Helm values or environment config.
- [ ] **Verify Docker build works end-to-end** — Run `docker build -f services/inventory-service/docker/Dockerfile .` from the repo root. The Dockerfile uses monorepo-relative `COPY` paths that haven't been validated in CI yet (CI only runs `dotnet build/test`, not `docker build`).
- [ ] **Angular `provideHttpClient()` bootstrap** — Confirm `main.ts` calls `provideHttpClient()` so the `HttpClient` injection in `InventoryListComponent` resolves at runtime. If missing, all HTTP calls will throw a runtime error.

**Recommended test plan:**
1. `dotnet test services/inventory-service/InventoryService.sln` — should pass 9/9
2. `dotnet run --project services/inventory-service/src/InventoryService.Api --urls http://localhost:5001` — hit `GET /health`, `GET /api/inventory`, `POST /api/inventory/product/1/deduct` with `{"quantity":1}`
3. Start the monolith (from the companion PR) on port 5000 and create an order — verify it calls inventory-service for stock check/deduction
4. `helm template test services/inventory-service/helm/inventory-service/ -f services/inventory-service/helm/inventory-service/values-dev.yaml` — verify templates render without errors

### Notes
- The `InventoryItem` model is intentionally decoupled from the monolith's `Product` entity — it carries its own `ProductName` and `Sku` fields for bounded context independence.
- Seed data initialization (`SeedData.Initialize`) should be idempotent — verify it checks for existing records before inserting to avoid duplicates on pod restarts.

Link to Devin session: https://partner-workshops.devinenterprise.com/sessions/8e5fd9d144fe4d368ae30e37a95cd7c0

author: copilot
body:
No test coverage existed for the full matrix of `TracingMode` (DEFAULT, TRACING, NEW_TRACING, ONNXSCRIPT) × `ConvertingLibrary` (DEFAULT, ONNXSCRIPT) against a minimal model.

## Changes

- **`_LinearModel` fixture** — module-level `nn.Linear`-only model added alongside the existing `_Neuron`, used as the shared input for all combination tests.

- **`TestTracingModeCombinationsLinear`** — new test class covering the meaningful combinations:

| Test | TracingMode | ConvertingLibrary | Strategy |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_linear_default_default` | DEFAULT | DEFAULT | full `to_onnx` — asserts valid `ModelProto` (1 input, 1 output) + numerical discrepancy check |
| `test_linear_tracing_default` | TRACING | DEFAULT | full `to_onnx` + numerical discrepancy check |
| `test_linear_new_tracing_default` | NEW_TRACING | DEFAULT | full `to_onnx` + numerical discrepancy check |
| `test_linear_default_onnxscript` | DEFAULT | ONNXSCRIPT | full `to_onnx` — asserts valid `ModelProto` |
| `test_linear_tracing_onnxscript` | TRACING | ONNXSCRIPT | skipped — onnxscript does not support fx.graph |
| `test_linear_new_tracing_onnxscript` | NEW_TRACING | ONNXSCRIPT | skipped — onnxscript does not support fx.graph |
| `test_linear_onnxscript_onnxscript` | ONNXSCRIPT | ONNXSCRIPT | mocked `torch.onnx.export` — verifies `dynamo=True` routing (requires full dynamo stack) |

`ConvertingLibrary.DEFAULT` paths validate numerical correctness via `ExtendedReferenceEvaluator` (asserting outputs match PyTorch within `atol=1e-5`). `TracingMode.DEFAULT + ConvertingLibrary.ONNXSCRIPT` runs fully end-to-end: `ExportOptions.export()` produces a genuine `torch.export.ExportedProgram` passed to `torch.onnx.export(ExportedProgram)` without `dynamo=True`. The TRACING and NEW_TRACING + ONNXSCRIPT combinations are skipped because onnxscript does not support the fx.graph format those tracing modes produce. Only `TracingMode.ONNXSCRIPT` (which calls `torch.onnx.export` with `dynamo=True`) retains a mock to avoid requiring the full dynamo compilation stack.

- **`import onnx`** promoted to a top-level module import.
- **`from yobx.reference import ExtendedReferenceEvaluator`** added as a top-level import to support the discrepancy checks.

body:
This pull request introduces several enhancements and refactorings across the `datamint` package, focusing on improved API usability, modular dataset support, and better error handling. The most significant changes include new convenience methods for working with annotation specs, improved project creation logic, and enhancements to dataset modularity and serialization.

**API Improvements and Annotation Handling:**

* Added methods to `AnnotationSetsApi` and `ProjectsApi` for retrieving annotation specifications directly from annotation sets or projects, streamlining workflows that require annotation metadata. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-42eb0315980b1071787cbe8b70018e109310d0722dc6ac63a72973c661d8b245L2-R49) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-fe1a81784850b2834482dc4310ae015e6b32cae6ef23489b678ffe6ba96d8c78R256-R269)
* Enhanced `ProjectsApi.create()` to support an `exists_ok` parameter, allowing the method to return an existing project instead of raising an error if a project with the same name already exists. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-fe1a81784850b2834482dc4310ae015e6b32cae6ef23489b678ffe6ba96d8c78L51-R57) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-fe1a81784850b2834482dc4310ae015e6b32cae6ef23489b678ffe6ba96d8c78L63-R70) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-fe1a81784850b2834482dc4310ae015e6b32cae6ef23489b678ffe6ba96d8c78L74-R82) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-fe1a81784850b2834482dc4310ae015e6b32cae6ef23489b678ffe6ba96d8c78R93-R105) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-fe1a81784850b2834482dc4310ae015e6b32cae6ef23489b678ffe6ba96d8c78L103-R120)

**Dataset Modularity and API Initialization:**

* Updated `datamint/__init__.py` to support modular dataset classes (`ImageDataset`, `VolumeDataset`) and clarified legacy vs. new exports for easier future maintenance and usage.

**Inference and Model Deployment Enhancements:**

* Improved error handling in `DeployModelApi.get_by_id()` by validating UUIDs and providing more informative exceptions.
* Refined `InferenceApi.wait()` to update the provided `InferenceJob` in-place and improved the notification mechanism for job status updates. Also, aliased `predict` to `submit` for consistency. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-00e1f2ce4677ecf81aef5e10d4e2624f287b60f3e272493d4fdcc4e17725feebL163-R211) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-00e1f2ce4677ecf81aef5e10d4e2624f287b60f3e272493d4fdcc4e17725feebL216-R222) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-00e1f2ce4677ecf81aef5e10d4e2624f287b60f3e272493d4fdcc4e17725feebR402-R403)

**Serialization and DTO Clean-up:**

* Added `__getstate__` and `__setstate__` methods to `Api` for improved serialization and deserialization support, which is useful for pickling or distributed settings.
* Cleaned up DTO exports to remove duplicates and ensure correct listing.

**Format Detection:**

* Improved the fallback logic for MIME type detection and error handling for empty files. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-83a8236d9b9ee78db34a4bf61b0da151852459123f279b6aa13a8009248262ccL11-L16) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-83a8236d9b9ee78db34a4bf61b0da151852459123f279b6aa13a8009248262ccR686-R687) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-83a8236d9b9ee78db34a4bf61b0da151852459123f279b6aa13a8009248262ccR723-R724) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-83a8236d9b9ee78db34a4bf61b0da151852459123f279b6aa13a8009248262ccL735-R747)

These changes collectively improve the robustness, usability, and maintainability of the `datamint` codebase.

body: ## Summary Adds a standalone Inventory Microservice extracted from the monolith's inventory domain. This is a .NET 8 Web API with its own data store, Angular frontend, Docker/Helm/ArgoCD IaC, and CI/CD pipeline. **API Endpoints:** - `GET /api/inventory` — list all inventory - `GET /api/inventory/product/{productId}` — get by product - `POST /api/inventory/product/{productId}/restock` — restock - `GET /api/inventory/low-stock` — low-stock filter - `POST /api/inventory/product/{productId}/check-stock` — check availability - `POST /api/inventory/product/{productId}/deduct` — deduct stock **Key design decisions:** - `InventoryItem` model removes the `Product` navigation property; adds denormalized `ProductName` field - Service class renamed to `InventoryManager` to avoid namespace conflict with `InventoryService.Api.Services` - SQLite for local dev, configurable via `INVENTORY_DB_CONNECTION` env var - Health checks at `/healthz` and `/readyz`, Prometheus metrics at `/metrics` ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] **`Program.cs` always calls `UseSqlite()`** — the connection string is configurable but the provider is not. If prod needs PostgreSQL, the `Program.cs` needs a conditional provider switch. Verify this is acceptable or needs a fix before deployment. - [ ] **CI workflow `argocd-sync` job** does `sed` replacement on `values.yaml` and pushes back to the repo from the action — review for race conditions and verify the `git push` has proper permissions. The hardcoded AWS account ID (`599083837640`) and IAM role ARN in `ci.yaml` need validation. - [ ] **Helm `networkpolicy.yaml`** allows ingress from `decomposition-dev` namespace and egress to `database` pods — verify these match your actual cluster labels/namespaces. - [ ] **CORS is fully open** (`AllowAnyOrigin/Method/Header`) — acceptable for local dev but ensure this is locked down for staging/prod via Helm values or environment config. - [ ] **Run the service locally and test end-to-end** with the companion monolith refactoring PR. Suggested plan: 1. `cd inventory-service && dotnet run --project src/InventoryService.Api/InventoryService.Api.csproj` (port 5002) 2. `dotnet test inventory-service/tests/InventoryService.Api.Tests/` (12 tests should pass) 3. `curl http://localhost:5002/api/inventory` — verify seeded data returns 4. `curl -X POST http://localhost:5002/api/inventory/product/1/check-stock -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"quantity":5}'` — verify stock check 5. Verify `/healthz`, `/readyz`, and `/metrics` endpoints respond ### Notes - The service file is named `InventoryService.cs` but the class inside is `InventoryManager` due to the namespace conflict — this naming mismatch is intentional but worth noting for future maintainers. - Solution file GUIDs are manually generated (not from `dotnet new sln`), which is cosmetic but unusual. - This PR is one half of the decomposition — the companion monolith refactoring PR replaces direct DB access with HTTP calls to this service. ## Summary

- Add async counterparts (`async_` prefix) to all VM lifecycle methods across 8 files
- Existing sync API is 100% unchanged — zero breaking changes
- Enables parallel VM creation via `asyncio.gather()`: 50 VMs in ~30s instead of 25 minutes
- New `SmolVM.async_create_many()` class method for batch VM creation with bounded concurrency
- Async context manager (`async with SmolVM(config) as vm:`)

## Key Additions

| File | Async Methods Added |
|------|-------------------|
| `utils.py` | `async_run_command()` |
| `network.py` | 25 async methods (TAP, nftables, NAT, port forwarding) |

| `api.py` | `async_wait_for_socket()` |

# Batch creation (the killer feature)
vms = await SmolVM.async_create_many([cfg1, cfg2, cfg3], concurrency=10)

author: sclarkamlab
body:
## :id: Reference related issue. 

https://gravitee.atlassian.net/browse/AM-6745

## :pencil2: A description of the changes proposed in the pull request

**Bug:** When a user has a previous incomplete MFA email enrollment (factor stuck in `PENDING_ACTIVATION` state), all subsequent enrollment attempts fail permanently with `"Invalid 2FA code, not the same value"`, even when the user enters the correct OTP.

**Root cause:** The `MFAEnrollEndpoint` did not check for or clean up an existing `PENDING_ACTIVATION` factor before starting a new enrollment. The stale factor's shared secret conflicted with the newly generated OTP, causing verification to always fail.

**Fix:**
- Added `removePendingEnrolledFactor(userId, factorId)` to gateway `UserService` to remove a factor in `PENDING_ACTIVATION` state for a given user and factor type
- Updated `MFAEnrollEndpoint` to detect an existing `PENDING_ACTIVATION` factor before enrollment and remove it, allowing a fresh enrollment to proceed
- Added unit tests for both the service method and the endpoint logic
- Added an E2E integration test covering the full re-enrollment flow after an abandoned MFA attempt

## :memo: Test scenarios 

- **Unit test:** `UserServiceTest` — verifies `removePendingEnrolledFactor` removes the correct factor and calls the user repository
- **Unit test:** `MFAEnrollEndpointTest` — verifies the endpoint removes a stale `PENDING_ACTIVATION` factor before re-enrolling
- **E2E test:** `mfa-pending-activation-reset.spec.ts` — end-to-end test that simulates an abandoned MFA enrollment followed by a successful re-enrollment

## :computer: Add screenshots for UI

N/A — backend-only change, no UI modifications.

## :books: Any other comments that will help with documentation

The previous workaround was to manually remove the `PENDING_ACTIVATION` email factor from the database. This fix automates that cleanup during re-enrollment.

<!-- See https://github.com/guardian/recommendations/blob/main/pull-requests.md for recommendations on raising and reviewing pull requests. -->

## What does this change?

We needed to reconsider our approach to mise.  Initially, the intention was to provide a cache which could be re-used across multiple installations.  However, the mise installer is not sufficiently stable to do this.  In order to provide a stable, usable, install, we will now have a mise specific to the container.  In the case of devenv, this means up to ten minutes of downloads on a reasonable home connection, and more in a low bandwidth situation such as a cafe.

This PR therefore removes all mise mount instructions and simplifies the install script.  

Additionally, it was noticed that some tests were not actually running, so there are some tweaks to ensure the base64 scripts are now correctly checked.

- Builds `flightAvatars: Record<icao24, FriendAvatarInfo[]>` — multiple friends can share the same flight and their bubbles naturally cluster

Strengthen multisig guidance: timelocks, separation, address discipline, and key takeaways

---

Revises the multisig security framework based on lessons from real-world multisig operations and emerging risks. Adds a one-page key takeaways summary for quick reference.

### Key changes

- **Design principles**: Added "build in slowness by design," "constrain emergency powers," and "separate responsibilities across multisigs" as foundational principles
- **Timelock guidance**: Strengthened from "recommended" to "essential" for protocol admin multisigs. Added tiered duration guidance (long/medium/short/none) and a dedicated timelock monitoring section
- **Multisig separation**: New section on separating multisigs by function with common patterns and a separation table
- **Address discipline**: New sections on address book hygiene (never copy from explorer history) and permissionless Safe addition / address poisoning risks
- **Dedicated keys**: Expanded rationale for using separate keys per multisig (wallet clarity + blast radius containment)
- **Calldata decoding**: Expanded from brief mention to full section covering how calldata works, decoding steps, and common red flags
- **Delegated proposers**: Corrected and clarified why delegated proposers matter (first signer verification) and why final signer should avoid "sign and execute"
- **Solana differences**: New section on architectural differences from EVM for multisig verification
- **Access control inventory**: New guidance on maintaining a comprehensive inventory of all privileged roles, added structured fields to the registration template
- **Key takeaways page**: New one-page summary distilling the 11 most important principles with links to full sections

author: dgdavid
body:
This is the final PR of series of changes for reimplementing the network connection form using [TanStack Form](https://tanstack.com/form/). Built on top of #3353, it removes the old IP settings form and its dependencies, completes the field component set, improves the name auto-sync approach, and fixes a validation gap in advanced mode.

### Removal of IpSettingsForm

`IpSettingsForm` and its supporting components (`AddressesDataList`, `DnsDataList`, `DnsSearchDataList`, `IpAddressInput`, `IpPrefixInput`, and their tests) are deleted. The new `ConnectionForm` based on TanStack Form fully replaces them.

### Bug fix: address validation in advanced mode

Addresses are optional in advanced mode, but if entered they must still be valid. Previously only manual mode validated them, so invalid entries could silently reach the server. The fix ensures to also validate entries when they are present in advanced mode, even though none are required.

### `generateConnectionName` as a pure function

`useConnectionName` was a React hook that had no real React dependency: it computed a name from its arguments and returned a string. It has been replaced by `generateConnectionName`, a plain function in `src/utils/network.ts` that is easier to test and works anywhere without a component context.

### Name auto-sync via form-level listeners

The previous approach used `useStore` to watch binding fields and a `useEffect` to write the derived name back. Both are replaced by TanStack Form's own [`listeners` API](https://tanstack.com/form/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/listeners)), which is the idiomatic way to handle field side effects in this library.

The listener fires on mount and on every change and, as in previous approach, it skips the update when the name field is already dirty, [using `isDirty` rather than `isTouched`](https://tanstack.com/form/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/basic-concepts#field-state) so that focusing and blurring the field without typing does not stop auto-generation. [`dontRunListeners: true`](https://github.com/TanStack/form/blob/42761767cf0662559d4f2c1a51b45b3720dbd451/packages/form-core/src/FieldApi.ts#L1446-L1449) prevents the name write from re-triggering the listener.

### DropdownField rename

`ChoiceField` was renamed to `DropdownField` since the old name gave no hint about what kind of input it renders. The TSDoc now explains that the component uses a PatternFly menu-based combobox rather than a native `<select>`, why the keyboard interaction differs from what users may expect, and includes a TODO for implementing the W3C-recommended arrow-key compromise.

### TextField and CheckboxField

Two new field components following the same `useFieldContext` pattern as `DropdownField` and `ArrayField`:

- `TextField`: a text input that shows validation errors inline below the input.
- `CheckboxField`: a checkbox with an optional description.

Both are registered in `useAppForm` and wired into `ConnectionForm` (name field, DNS toggles) and `IpSettings` (gateway field), replacing the inline markup that was previously scattered across those components.

A `## Field component conventions` section was added to `form-contexts.ts` to document the shared contract: `onChange` is wired internally, `onBlur` is intentionally not wired (submit-only validation, revisit when a use case arises), and lifecycle events belong on `form.AppField` via `listeners`, not on the component itself.

### Action button form components

Two action button components are registered under `formComponents` so they are available on any typed form instance without form-specific wiring:

- `form.SubmitButton`: reads `isSubmitting` via `useFormContext` and renders a submit button that shows a loading indicator and disables itself while the form is submitting.
- `form.CancelButton`: encapsulates `navigate(-1)` via `useNavigate`, rendering a link button that returns to the previous page.

`ConnectionForm`'s action group reduces to:

```tsx
<ActionGroup>
  <form.SubmitButton />
  <form.CancelButton />
</ActionGroup>
```
### Form conventions update

`src/components/form/conventions.md` has been updated to reflect the implemented state of `ConnectionForm`. Stale notes are replaced with accurate descriptions, conditional rendering is consistently described as "not rendered" rather than "hidden" throughout, and a new Validation section explains the submit-only approach, the cross-field `onSubmitAsync` pattern, and the `setErrorMap` workaround needed to re-enable submission after a failed attempt.

### Notes for reviewers

Changelog entry postponed for the final PR from the feature branch against master.

body:
Shifts the platform to invite-only creator onboarding with Mochii as the default creator. Removes all self-service creator application surface area and consolidates login to a single form per audience.

## Creator Application Flow — Removed
- Deleted `POST /api/creator/apply` endpoint, `CreatorApplicationRequest` / `ApplicationApproveRequest` / `ApplicationRejectRequest` models, and all three admin review endpoints (`GET/POST /api/admin/creator-applications/{approve,reject}`) from `compliance.py`
- Removed orphaned imports (`uuid`, `urlparse`, `BackgroundTasks`) from `compliance.py`
- Dropped `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS creator_applications` from `main.py` startup (table preserved on disk for existing deployments)

## Primary Creator Constant
Replaced scattered `"mochii"` string fallbacks with a named `_PRIMARY_CREATOR = "mochii"` constant in each affected router:
- `routers/questions.py` — `PublicQuestion.creator_handle` default
- `routers/drool.py` — `DroolItem.creator_handle` default + row fallback
- `routers/admin.py` — `ProductCreate.creator_handle` default
- `routers/subscriptions.py` — Segpay webhook tier-miss fallback

Added comments in `main.py` migration block clarifying `'mochii'` column defaults as the platform primary creator.

## Landing / Explore
- `landing.html`: removed "Become a Creator →" hero CTA, `.btn-hero-ghost` CSS, creator-pitch section + CSS, footer "Become a Creator" link
- `explore.html`: removed "✨ Featured Creators" section, `renderCreators()` function, and its `loadExplore()` call — featured-creator queue API is retained for admin spotlight use

## Login Consolidation
- `index.html` (subscriber portal): removed "Creator" tab, `#creator-login-form`, `#creator-otp-form`, `handleCreatorLogin()`, `handleCreatorOtp()`, `_creatorPendingToken`, and the creator-branch in `switchAuthTab()` — auth card is now Sign In / Register only

Admin creator management CRUD, Cloudflare subdomain provisioning, featured-creator queue, and all payment/streaming/member portal machinery are unchanged.

## Summary

When using a routing provider like `openrouter/auto`, the configured model name and the model actually selected at runtime differ. Previously there was no visibility into which model was chosen.

author: fredrik3b
body:
# Refactor auth store & onboarding flow
 
## Summary
 
Rewrites the auth store to fix state bugs causing blank-page crashes, adds a backend endpoint for pending join requests, and splits the onboarding view into smaller components.
 

 
## Backend
 
**New endpoint:** `GET /api/organizations/join-request` returns the user's pending join request (`200` with body) or `204` if none exists. Replaces client-side guesswork about pending state.
 
**Files:** `OrganizationController`, `OrganizationService`, `OrganizationMapper`, new `JoinRequestResponse` DTO.
 
 
## Frontend

### Auth Store
 
**Removed** redundant state: `restaurantStatus`, `restaurantId`, `restaurantName`, `restaurantJoinCode`, these were a conflicting mix of refs and computeds (some actions silently failed assigning to computeds).
 
**Replaced with:**
- `restaurant` (single ref, from backend) + `pendingRequest` (fetched via the new endpoint)
- `hasActiveRestaurant` / `hasPendingRequest` computeds
 
**Fixed:**
- `!!restaurant.value.id` to `!!restaurant.value?.id`, the null dereference that crashed the entire app
- `initAuth` no longer wraps synchronous localStorage reads in unnecessary promises
- `_saveSession` auto-clears pending state when the backend returns a restaurant
- Pending state is fetched from the backend on init
 
 
### Onboarding View
 
Split the big `RestaurantOnboardingView.vue` into:
 
| Component | Responsibility |
|-----------|---------------|
| `RestaurantOnboardingView.vue` | Orchestrator — view switching + stepper |
| `OnboardingTopbar.vue` | Header with user info + logout |
| `OnboardingChoose.vue` | Join vs create selection |
| `OnboardingJoin.vue` | Join code input form |
| `OnboardingPending.vue` | Pending status, check button, withdraw |
 
Added a `watch` on `hasPendingRequest` so the pending view shows correctly after page refresh (previously defaulted to "choose" because the async fetch hadn't resolved yet).

author: jwfraustro
body:
lxml6 removed support for automatically resolving URL's in schema files, which was necessary to import the remove IVOA schemas that comprised ones being tested in this package. (`VODataService <- VOResource`).

```
Binary wheels use the library versions libxml2 2.14.4 and libxslt 1.1.43. Note that this disables direct HTTP and FTP support for parsing from URLs. Use Python URL request tools instead (which usually also support HTTPS). To test the availability, use "http" in etree.LIBXML_FEATURES.
```

To support this feature, I've added a simple URL resolver to replace the one in lxml.etree, to still be able to handle these linked remote schemas.

author: hanouticelina
body:
Fixes #4050.

when passing a custom `tqdm_class` to `hf_hub_download()` or `snapshot_download()`, progress tracking is broken. this is because all tqdm classes are instantiated identically. When a user passes a custom `tqdm_class`, they take full control of progress bar behavior. The library should not inject HF-specific kwargs (`name`) or override display logic (`disable`).  the custom class is responsible for its own configuration.
Here is a small reproducible:
```python
from tqdm.auto import tqdm
from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download


class MyProgress(tqdm):
    def update(self, n=1):
        super().update(n)
        print(f"Progress: {self.n}/{self.total}")


hf_hub_download(
    repo_id="unsloth/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-GGUF",
    filename="config.json",
    tqdm_class=MyProgress,
    force_download=True,
)
```

this causes two bugs depending on the environment:

In TTY: `disable=None` -> `isatty()` returns `True` -> tqdm continues `__init__` -> hits the unknown kwargs check → `TqdmKeyError` on `name`:

```
python reproducible.py
  ...
  File "huggingface_hub/utils/tqdm.py", line 300, in _get_progress_bar_context
    return (tqdm_class or tqdm)(
    ...
tqdm.std.TqdmKeyError: "Unknown argument(s): {'name': 'huggingface_hub.http_get'}"
```

In non-TTY: `is_tqdm_disabled()` returns `None`. Vanilla tqdm interprets `disable=None` as "check `sys.stderr.isatty()`" → `False` in non-TTY → sets `self.disable = True` → `update()` becomes a no-op. No crash, but progress is silently lost:

```
$ python reproducible.py 2>&1 | cat
Progress: 0/None
```

⚠️ BREAKING CHANGE: custom `tqdm_class` instances no longer receive the `name` kwarg or `disable` value, the custom class is fully responsible for its own configuration. 

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Low risk: change is isolated to progress bar instantiation logic and adds regression tests; main behavior change only affects callers providing a custom `tqdm_class`, especially in non-TTY environments.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes progress reporting when callers pass a custom `tqdm_class` by centralizing progress-bar creation in `_create_progress_bar` and only applying Hugging Face–specific kwargs (`name`) and disable/TTY logic for the HF `tqdm` subclass.
> 
> Updates both `_get_progress_bar_context` and `snapshot_download` to use this helper, and adds regression tests to ensure group-based disabling still works for HF bars while vanilla/custom tqdm classes are neither force-disabled in non-TTY nor passed the unsupported `name` kwarg.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit d5d3eba80b862b84f16f3118bec3a25ba49852dd. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

author: semgrep-code-zpgeng[bot]
body:
Fix SQL injection vulnerability in the `/unsafe-search` endpoint by using parameterized queries instead of string interpolation.

## Changes
- Replaced f-string SQL query with parameterized query using named placeholder `:pattern`
- Added `pattern` variable to safely construct the search pattern
- Passed parameters to `db.execute()` as a dictionary for safe binding

## Why
The original code directly interpolated user input `q` into the SQL query string using an f-string (`WHERE title LIKE '%{q}%'`). This allowed attackers to inject arbitrary SQL by crafting malicious search queries.

Using SQLAlchemy's parameterized queries ensures user input is properly escaped by the database driver, preventing SQL injection attacks while maintaining the same search functionality.

## Semgrep Finding Details
Untrusted input might be used to build a database query, which can lead to a SQL injection vulnerability. An attacker can execute malicious SQL statements and gain unauthorized access to sensitive data, modify, delete data, or execute arbitrary system commands. The driver API has the ability to bind parameters to the query in a safe way. Make sure not to dynamically create SQL queries from user-influenced inputs. If you cannot avoid this, either escape the data properly or create an allowlist to check the value.

@22430359 requested Semgrep Assistant generate this pull request to fix [a finding](https://semgrep.dev/orgs/fred_guazipi/findings/742852279) from the detection rule [python.fastapi.db.generic-sql-fastapi.generic-sql-fastapi](https://semgrep.dev/r/python.fastapi.db.generic-sql-fastapi.generic-sql-fastapi).

author: dawoudio
body:
## Summary

- Inline `onclick` attributes on Delete buttons in the three custom field editors (Group, Family, Person) are blocked when CSP is enforced (`script-src` does not include `unsafe-inline`)
- Replaces `onclick="confirmDeleteField(...)"` with `data-field-name`, `data-field-id` (and `data-prop-id` for Group) attributes on the button
- Adds a delegated `$(document).on('click', '.js-delete-field')` listener inside the **existing** `<script nonce="...">` block — no new script tags
- Removes the now-unnecessary `$fieldNameJs`/`$fieldIdJs` PHP intermediary variables

## Why

ChurchCRM's `Content-Security-Policy` `script-src` directive does not include `unsafe-inline`. When `bEnforceCSP` is enabled, all inline event handlers are silently blocked. Discovered during review of #8509 (which patched only the HTML-attribute quoting in `GroupPropsFormEditor.php`).

This fix makes Delete work under both report-only **and** enforced CSP, and is consistent with the pattern documented in `security-best-practices.md` → _No Inline Event Handlers_.

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/GroupPropsFormEditor.php` | `onclick` → `data-field-name/prop-id/field-id` + delegated listener |
| `src/FamilyCustomFieldsEditor.php` | `onclick` → `data-field-name/field-id` + delegated listener |
| `src/PersonCustomFieldsEditor.php` | `onclick` → `data-field-name/field-id` + delegated listener |
| `cypress/e2e/ui/admin/person-custom-fields.spec.js` | Regression tests for Person + Family delete buttons |
| `cypress/e2e/ui/groups/standard.group.properties.spec.js` | Regression test for Group props form delete button |

## Testing

Cypress regression tests added that verify for all three editors:
1. Delete button has `data-field-name`/`data-field-id` attributes and **no** `onclick`
2. Clicking the button opens the bootbox confirm dialog (event delegation fires)
3. Cancel leaves the field intact
4. Confirm deletes the field and shows a success notification

Manual steps:
1. Open Admin → Custom Fields (Person, Family, Group)
2. Click the ⋮ menu on any field → **Delete** — confirm dialog should appear and delete should succeed
3. Enable `bEnforceCSP` in System Settings → repeat above — Delete must still work (no CSP console errors)

## Related Issues

- Fixes #8508
- Supersedes #8509 (the `htmlspecialchars(json_encode(...))` workaround is no longer needed since the `onclick` attribute is removed entirely)

author: aaronbrezel
body:
## Summary

- Replaces `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive` with `drive.readonly` + `drive.file` in `appsscript.json`, removing "See, edit, create, and delete all of your Google Drive files" from the consent screen
- Adds `docs/auth-model.md` — user-facing permissions guide explaining what each scope allows and cannot do
- Adds `docs/plans/2026-04-02-least-privilege-auth-design.md` — design doc covering rationale, rejected alternatives (Picker-only, Service Account Bridge), operation-to-scope mapping, and manual test plan

## Why these two scopes

`drive.readonly` covers all read operations (folder scanning, file metadata, file content for Extract Text and Run AI). `drive.file` covers the one write operation that remains: creating and deleting the temporary Google Doc used for PDF/image OCR in Extract Text. No existing functionality is affected.

## What was considered and rejected

- **`drive.file` only + Google Picker**: `drive.file` does not grant access to children of a selected folder, breaking recursive folder scanning in Import Drive Links.
- **Service Account Bridge**: Introduces persistent ACL entries on user files, requires service account credential management, and would be blocked by the org Drive sharing policies that motivated this change.
- **`spreadsheets.currentonly`**: Run AI's multi-sheet Sheets file export requires `SpreadsheetApp.openById()` — deferred.
- **Eliminating `documents` scope**: Existing code comment warns `Drive.Files.export()` returns metadata not content in the Advanced Service — safe alternative deferred.

## GCP Console change required

The Workspace Marketplace SDK App Configuration (OAuth Scopes section) must be updated manually to match:
- Replace `auth/drive` with `auth/drive.readonly`
- Add `auth/drive.file`

## Test plan

- [x] Deploy to test instance
- [x] Import Drive Links: recursive folder scan writes URLs to sheet
- [x] Extract Text (Google Doc): reads doc body text
- [x] Extract Text (PDF/image): creates temp doc, OCR, deletes temp doc
- [x] Run AI (text columns): batch inference writes to sheet
- [x] Run AI (Drive file inputs — Doc, PDF, image): fetches and encodes file

author: copilot
body:
Docker image publishing was blocked by two independent failures: `uv` was not available in the dependencies stage, and Python dependency resolution was unsatisfiable in the LangChain/Ollama stack. This PR aligns install mechanics and version bounds so the Docker workflow can resolve and build consistently.

- **Root-cause alignment**
  - Replace shell-based UV install with a deterministic Python install in the base image.
  - Remove conflicting package combination (`ollama-python` + `langchain-ollama` with mismatched `httpx` expectations).

- **Dependency graph normalization**
  - Tighten LangChain family ranges across dependency sources:
    - `langchain>=0.2.17,<0.3.0`
    - `langchain-community>=0.2.17,<0.3.0`
    - `langchain-ollama>=0.1.3,<0.2.0`
  - Update constraints to `httpx==0.27.2` to match the selected LangChain/Ollama line.
  - Apply the same bounds in `requirements.txt`, `constraints.txt`, and `pyproject.toml` to avoid drift.

- **Docker build behavior**
  - Keep dependency installation in Docker on `uv pip install --system -r requirements.txt`, with UV now guaranteed present in later stages.

```dockerfile
# before
RUN curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

# after
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir uv
```

author: copilot
body:
`src/api/datasets/operations.ts` used `console.debug()` directly, unconditionally printing to stdout — including SAS URIs containing secret tokens. All SDK logging must go through `@azure/logger` so output is gated behind `AZURE_LOG_LEVEL` and never surfaces in production by default.

### Changes

- **`src/api/datasets/operations.ts`**
  - Added import for the package's existing logger: `import { logger } from "../../logger.js"`
  - Replaced all 8 `console.debug(...)` calls with `logger.verbose(...)`:
    - 6 in `createDatasetAndGetItsContainer()` — one of which logged `blobReference.credential.sasUri` (raw SAS token)
    - 2 in `uploadFolder()` — file upload progress
- **`CHANGELOG.md`** — Added a `Bugs Fixed` entry under the `2.0.2 (2026-04-06)` section (empty sections removed).
- **`package.json`** / **`src/constants.ts`** — Bumped package version from `2.0.1` → `2.0.2` (patch).

```ts
// Before — always prints to console, leaks secrets
console.debug(`[createDatasetAndGetItsContainer] blobReference.credential.sasUri = ${blobReference.credential.sasUri}`);

// After — only emits when AZURE_LOG_LEVEL=verbose is explicitly set
logger.verbose(`[createDatasetAndGetItsContainer] blobReference.credential.sasUri = ${blobReference.credential.sasUri}`);
```

### Packages impacted by this PR

`@azure/ai-projects`

### Issues associated with this PR

`@azure/ai-projects` leaks secrets via `console.debug` in `src/api/datasets/operations.ts`.

### Describe the problem that is addressed by this PR

`console.debug` calls in the datasets operations file emit unconditionally to stdout regardless of environment or log-level configuration, exposing SAS URI secrets in any environment where the code runs.

### What are the possible designs available to address the problem? If there are more than one possible design, why was the one in this PR chosen?

The only correct fix is to route all logging through the package's existing `@azure/logger` instance. Using `logger.verbose()` matches the debug intent and ensures output is opt-in via `AZURE_LOG_LEVEL`.

### Are there test cases added in this PR? _(If not, why?)_

No. The change is a mechanical substitution of logging calls; existing tests cover the surrounding logic. The security property (no unconditional console output) is enforced structurally.

### Provide a list of related PRs _(if any)_

None.

- [x] Added impacted package name to the issue description
- [ ] Does this PR needs any fixes in the SDK Generator?** _(If so, create an Issue in the [Autorest/typescript](https://github.com/Azure/autorest.typescript) repository and link it here)_
- [x] Added a changelog (if necessary)

author: rammicz
body:
## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip orchestrates AI agents for zero-human companies
> - Agents pick up issues by checking them out, which sets execution locks on the issue (`executionRunId`, `executionLockedAt`, `executionAgentNameKey`)
> - When something goes wrong or a user wants to retry, they can reset an issue back to "todo" status
> - The reset path was already clearing `assigneeAgentId` and `checkoutRunId` but not the execution state fields
> - This meant stale execution locks remained on the issue after reset
> - Other agents seeing the stale lock would skip the issue, thinking it was still being worked on
> - This pull request adds clears for `executionRunId`, `executionLockedAt`, and `executionAgentNameKey` to the reset path
> - The benefit is that reset issues are fully clean and can be picked up by agents again without manual database intervention

## What Changed

- Clear `executionRunId`, `executionLockedAt`, and `executionAgentNameKey` alongside the existing `assigneeAgentId` and `checkoutRunId` clears when resetting an issue to "todo" in `server/src/services/issues.ts`
- Added integration test in `server/src/__tests__/issues-service.test.ts` verifying all execution state fields are nulled on release

## Verification

- Run the new test: `npx vitest run server/src/__tests__/issues-service.test.ts`
- Reset an in-progress issue to "todo" and verify all three execution fields are null in the database
- Confirm the reset issue can be checked out and picked up by an agent again

## Risks

Low risk — additive null-setting on an existing reset path. No schema changes, no new queries, no behavioral change for issues that aren't being reset.

## Model Used

Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) — `claude-opus-4-6`, tool use mode via Claude Code CLI

## Summary
  Formalizes the runtime check contract and adds an acceptance matrix that verifies runtime truth stays aligned across choices, adventure context, and prompt output.

  ## What changed
  - defined the runtime check contract explicitly in project docs
  - added acceptance tests that verify the same runtime state across:
    - `buildAvailableChoices`
    - `buildRelevantAdventureContext`
    - `buildSystemPrompt`
  - removed runtime free-text check inference from the runtime resolver
  - added explicit authored `check` blocks for investigative runtime interactions that should be probe-based
  - added regression coverage for the UI contract:
    - runtime choices render as check-based only when the resolved authored interaction defines `check`

  ## Runtime check contract
  - runtime-module checks come from explicit authored `interaction.check` data only
  - runtime choices may render as check-based only when the resolved authored runtime interaction defines `check`
  - no runtime check inference from free text or AI tags
  - legacy/prose adventures still keep AI-tag and label-based fallback behavior

  ## Why
  The goal is to keep runtime modules fully engine-authoritative.

  Before this change, runtime probe behavior was partly implicit:
  - some checks came from authored module data
  - some behavior still depended on residual free-text heuristics
  - the UI contract for blue/check-based runtime options was not explicitly documented

  This branch makes the rule explicit and testable:
  - blue means authored runtime check
  - not “sounds risky”
  - not AI-authored
  - not inferred from prompt wording or typed text

  ## Tests
  - added runtime acceptance matrix coverage
  - added runtime check contract regressions

body:
This pull request introduces major enhancements to support email campaign functionality (using the Resend API), improves restaurant access control, and adds several new models and configuration options. It also updates the database initialization to support new email-related collections, refines super admin access logic, and updates application branding and configuration for the DishPatch product.

**Email Campaigns and Models**

* Added new Pydantic models for email campaigns (`email_campaign.py`), email logs (`email_log.py`), and email templates (`email_template.py`) to support the new email channel and related API endpoints. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-13899897b54f97aad86755a026ad85ea3c7a2ff7b9f05b206ceb05c103ffbbd7R1-R57) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-bcd6314a293ede23647240fb84d4b35b0f23aaf172a2e162eee1918aaab34c15R1-R45) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-dc0f8bf0648a866b74e0d1206cd1136095c56b66bea4ccf9534712a145c57c47R1-R41)
* Introduced `ResendAPIError` in `errors.py` for handling errors from the Resend email API.
* Updated `config.py` to include Resend (email) configuration options such as API key, webhook secret, sender email, and rate limit.

**Database and Indexing**

* Enhanced `database.py` to dynamically resolve the MongoDB database name from the connection URL or config, and to initialize indexes for new email-related collections (campaigns, logs, templates, suppression list, webhook events). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e1abb886c86ecae873f8e9ba189818177f3e45b62120630b776b172bc3f1cf61R4-R23) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e1abb886c86ecae873f8e9ba189818177f3e45b62120630b776b172bc3f1cf61L16-R40) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-e1abb886c86ecae873f8e9ba189818177f3e45b62120630b776b172bc3f1cf61R131-R186)

**Restaurant Access and Roles**

* Improved super admin logic in `dependencies.py` to return all possible restaurant identifiers (both slug and ObjectId) and standardized access checks for regular users.

**Configuration and Branding**

* Changed application name and branding in `.env.example` and `main.py` from "WA Bulk Sender" to "DishPatch", and updated the API title accordingly. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a3046da0d15a27e89f2afe639b25748a7ad4d9290af3e7b1b6c1a5533c8f0a8cL37-R46) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c37e8fdac63710bdce2b091df72abe8ea2ca532980c6ad2886156bf1af5b4422L38-R45)
* Added configuration for the ReserveGo upload portal and its credentials in both `.env.example` and `config.py`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a3046da0d15a27e89f2afe639b25748a7ad4d9290af3e7b1b6c1a5533c8f0a8cL37-R46) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-667a1176a45630b7bfaea3fbb5838ce33e3b43b02204ad8dffed18eb182a1f9eR63-R66)

**API and Router Integration**

* Registered new routers for email campaigns, email templates, admin, and ReserveGo upload portal in `main.py`, making the new endpoints available. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c37e8fdac63710bdce2b091df72abe8ea2ca532980c6ad2886156bf1af5b4422R23-R25) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c37e8fdac63710bdce2b091df72abe8ea2ca532980c6ad2886156bf1af5b4422R89) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-c37e8fdac63710bdce2b091df72abe8ea2ca532980c6ad2886156bf1af5b4422R101-R103)
* Updated Celery worker queues to include the "email" queue for processing email jobs.

Other notable changes:

* Added a `parent_campaign_id` field to WhatsApp campaign responses for tracking retries.
* Updated `RestaurantResponse` to include `member_categories` and added a request model for updating categories.
* Updated member type to be a string for future extensibility.
* Minor improvements to JWT decoding, campaign creation defaults, and inbox message status tracking. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-118ad9bb7ddf882244219c29de4269270cec54c7f518520d5a9d0def43bf5103L40-R42) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-71bcb85428ba2ea2b9fd81aa93652fe8a682947b6e4eafc23e4916101f129badL17-R19) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-023cbdd4aa2b2ede61da6523958e5e07f7de6b6b14c00b3563ecb630fab1278aR29)

author: marcoteix
body:
### Summary

- Replaces the fixed --min-ani threshold with a data-driven outlier filter controlled by a single --alpha parameter (default: 10).
- For each sample, the highest ANI it shares with any other sample is compared against median - alpha × IQR of all pairwise ANIs. Samples below this threshold have their sample-private variants replaced with the per-site consensus, matching the previous behaviour.
- Larger alpha values are more permissive (only extreme divergent outliers are filtered); smaller values increase sensitivity.
- Documents the cleansweep collection command and the new filter in the README.

### Changed files

File | Change
-- | --
cleansweep/collection.py | Replaced min_ani field and fixed-threshold logic with alpha-based IQR outlier detection; removed unused use_core method
cleansweep/cli/collection.py | Replaced --min-ani/-a with --alpha/-a; updated log message
tests/test_collection.py | Updated test invocation to --alpha 10; removed unused import
README.md | Added cleansweep collection usage section with explanation of the filter

### Algorithm change
**Before:** each sample's mean SNP distance to all other samples was converted to an ANI estimate and compared against a fixed --min-ani threshold (default 0.995). Samples below the threshold had sample-private variants replaced with the per-site consensus.

**After:** 

1. All pairwise ANIs are computed from the SNP distance matrix: `ANI(i,j) = 1 - SNP_distance(i,j) / genome_length`.
2. The median and IQR of all pairwise ANIs (upper triangle) are computed.
3. A dynamic threshold is set: `threshold = median - alpha × IQR`.
4. For each sample, its maximum ANI to any other sample is checked. If it falls below the threshold, the sample is flagged as a divergent outlier and its sample-private variants are replaced with the per-site consensus.
5. This avoids the need to choose a meaningful absolute ANI cutoff, which varies with genome size and evolutionary distance. The `alpha` parameter only needs to express how many IQRs below the median counts as an outlier, which is dataset-agnostic.

author: btli
body:
## Summary

- Fix combined `grid_voltage` and `eps_voltage` sensors showing "Unknown" on US split-phase inverters (12kPV, FlexBOSS, etc.)
- Add L1+L2 fallback in `alias_common_voltage_sensors()` when R-phase register is None
- 7 new tests covering all fallback scenarios

## Root Cause

`alias_common_voltage_sensors()` only copied from R-phase registers (`grid_voltage_r` → `grid_voltage`), but R/S/T phase registers contain garbage on US split-phase systems. Since `grid_voltage_r` was always None for these devices, the combined sensor was never populated.

## Fix

When R-phase is None, fall back to summing L1+L2 phase voltages:
- `grid_voltage = grid_voltage_l1 + grid_voltage_l2` (~240V for split-phase)
- `eps_voltage = eps_voltage_l1 + eps_voltage_l2` (~240V for split-phase)

Handles edge cases: single-leg only, both legs None, R-phase precedence preserved for three-phase.

## Test plan

- [x] 7 new tests for L1+L2 fallback, R-phase precedence, single-leg, no-data
- [x] 822 tests pass (full suite)
- [x] ruff check + format clean
- [x] mypy strict pass

author: szmyd
body:
## Summary

Adds static estimation methods to calculate worst-case memory usage **before** RAID device construction. This enables external services (e.g., gRPC handlers) to validate memory availability against cgroup limits before creating RAID devices, preventing OOM scenarios.

Key improvement: **Layered API** separates target-level (queue/thread) overhead from device-specific overhead, avoiding double-counting when devices are stacked.

## Memory Components Estimated

**Target Level** (shared across device stack):
- **ublksrv I/O buffers**: `(qdepth × max_io_size)` per queue (~64 MiB default)
- **Thread stacks**: 8 MiB per queue (OS default)
- **Target overhead**: ~4 KiB

**Device Level** (RAID-specific):
- **RAID-1**: SuperBlocks + worst-case bitmap (100% dirty pages, scales with volume size)

## API

```cpp
// Target-level: queue and thread overhead (reads runtime config from SISL options)
uint64_t ublkpp_tgt::estimate_queue_memory() noexcept;

// RAID-1: device-specific overhead (reads chunk_size from SISL options)
uint64_t Raid1Disk::estimate_device_overhead(uint64_t volume_size) noexcept;
```

**Why layered?** In stacked configurations (e.g., RAID-0 → RAID-1 → FSDisk), queue memory is allocated once at the target level and shared. Device overhead is specific to each RAID layer.

## Implementation Details

- Uses `sizeof(Bitmap::PageData)` with compile-time verification via `static_assert`
- Removed magic numbers in favor of `sizeof` for maintainability
- Runtime config (qdepth, max_io_size, nr_hw_queues, chunk_size) read from SISL options
- Only truly dynamic parameters (volume_size, num_disks) passed to methods
- Worst-case bitmap estimation for conservative safety
- All methods are `noexcept` static functions

## Recent Changes

**Use `sizeof` instead of magic numbers** (commits 4cdd316, 598041b):
- Replaced hardcoded `k_page_data_overhead` constant with `sizeof(raid1::Bitmap::PageData)`
- Added `static_assert(sizeof(raid1::Bitmap::PageData) == 24)` to catch structure changes at compile time
- Updated tests to use exact values (`EXPECT_EQ`) instead of ranges, now that size is guaranteed

This makes the code more robust: if PageData structure changes in the future, the build will fail with a clear error message prompting an update to the memory estimation.

## Test Coverage

- ✅ **6 unit tests** (5 RAID-1, 1 target)
- ✅ Exact value assertions for all memory calculations
- ✅ Volume size scaling (bitmap growth)
- ✅ Linear scaling validation (10x volume = ~10x memory)
- ✅ Edge cases (single disk, small/large volumes)
- ✅ All tests pass with address sanitizer

## Example Usage

```cpp
// In gRPC service handling RAID-1 creation requests
uint64_t total_memory = 
    ublkpp::ublkpp_tgt::estimate_queue_memory() +           // ~72 MiB (default config)
    ublkpp::Raid1Disk::estimate_device_overhead(volume_size); // ~4-40 MiB (1-10 TiB)

uint64_t available_memory = probe_cgroup_memory_available();
if (total_memory > available_memory) {
    return grpc::Status(grpc::StatusCode::RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED,
                       fmt::format("Insufficient memory: need {} MiB, have {} MiB",
                                 total_memory / (1024 * 1024),
                                 available_memory / (1024 * 1024)));
}

// Safe to create
auto raid1 = std::make_unique<ublkpp::Raid1Disk>(...);
```

## Known Limitations

1. **ublksrv buffer estimate**: Formula-based approximation (no API available to query actual size)
2. **Thread stack assumption**: Hardcoded 8 MiB (Linux default), may vary by OS
3. **Bitmap worst-case**: Assumes 100% dirty pages - may over-estimate by up to 10x in practice
4. **Static only**: Estimate is pre-construction; doesn't track runtime growth

These limitations are acceptable for OOM prevention use case, where conservative estimates are preferred.

## Test Results

All tests passing with exact value verification:
```
Target:  1/1 tests passed
RAID-1:  5/5 tests passed
```

**Example estimates** (default config: qdepth=128, max_io=512KiB, nr_queues=1):
- Queue overhead: ~72 MiB
- RAID-1 (512 MiB): 12,312 bytes (exact)
- RAID-1 (1 TiB): 4,227,072 bytes (exact)
- RAID-1 (10 TiB): 42,196,992 bytes (exact)

body: ## Repackage `arc` as replan_central Python package This PR migrates the `arc` flight software from a project installed with a Makefile under `$SKA_SHARE/arc3` into a proper Python package (replan_central) installable via pyproject.toml, with Perl scripts bundled as package data. ### Packaging - All Python scripts are now modules under replan_central, each with a `main()` entry point registered as a console script (e.g. `replan-central-make-timeline`). - Perl scripts and config/data files are bundled under perl and data respectively, located at runtime via `importlib.resources` and `FindBin`. - task_schedule.cfg updated to invoke all tasks via the new entry point names and `$ENV{SKA}/data` paths. ### Output directory separation Scripts that previously wrote outputs into the same directory as their input data now accept a separate `--out` argument: - make_timeline.py — `timeline.png`, `timeline_states.js`, `comms_avail.html` now go to `--out` (web dir) instead of `--data-dir` (data dir). - get_hrc.py — `hrc_shield.dat`, `p4gm.dat`, `p41gm.dat` go to `--out`. - plot_goes_x.py, plot_hrc.py — `--out` renamed to `--out-file`; parent directories created automatically. - get_solar_flare_png.py — output parent directory created automatically. - arc.pl — takes explicit `--out` and `--data_dir` args instead of deriving paths from `$SKA_DATA`/`$SKA_SHARE` env vars. The now-redundant copy of `timeline.png` and `timeline_states.js` from data dir to web dir is removed since make_timeline.py writes them directly to `--out`. ### Perl de-globalization and config path fixes All Perl scripts (arc.pl, get_iFOT_events.pl, get_web_content.pl, arc_time_machine.pl) converted from `our` to `my` scope, moved from env-var-derived config paths to `FindBin`-relative paths into the bundled `data/` directory. ### arc_time_machine.pl: Mercurial → Git The iFOT time machine repository is now managed with Git instead of Mercurial. Each run commits and tags with a timestamp of the form `YYYY-MM-DDTHHMMSS` to ensure uniqueness across multiple runs per day. The time machine directory is created automatically if it does not exist. Mercurial/hg was no longer available on kady. ### make_timeline.py: remove fluence percentile plot The 10th/50th/90th percentile fluence projection lines (previously green/blue/red) have been intentionally removed from the timeline plot. The associated `--max-slope-samples`, `--min-flux-samples` arguments and `get_p3_slope()` helper are removed. The `calc_fluence_dist` dependency is dropped. ## Interface impacts As noted, the fluence percentiles have been removed from the "timeline" plot near the top of the page. The ops.html version of the page, previously available at https://cxc.cfa.harvard.edu/mta/ASPECT/arc3/ops.html will be removed and not supported. ## Testing Has been running "on-the-side" with output to: https://cxc.cfa.harvard.edu/mta/ASPECT/arc3_pip_test/ There are "snapshot" diffs at https://icxc.cfa.harvard.edu/aspect/test_review_outputs/replan_central/pr1/diffs/ And there's an example of a timeline plot generated from historical higher-radiation data at https://icxc.cfa.harvard.edu/aspect/test_review_outputs/replan_central/pr1/historical_timeline/2026_093_13/timeline.png which is qualitatively similar to the plot Tom put in slack on day 093: Confirmed manually that GOES.h5 ACE.h5 hrc_shield.h5 have basically identical values between the on-the-side processing and flight. I ignored trailing row mismatches due to staggered update times. I used a start date of 2026:001 for the check (the on-the-side job has been running for months at this point). In the diffs I noted that a single sample in the flight hrc_shield.h5 data at 2026:187:01:25:00.000 on the p3 column had the BAD value of -100000.0 and the test data had the real value of 0.1615741493878886. My only conjecture for this is that NOAA may have updated the bad value to a real value after the flight data had been updated and before the test data had been updated. We could consider an update to the hrc shield data processing to do a diff/lookback for any recent corrections from NOAA. Additionally, in the ACE data, the test file has two rows not present in flight: ``` Inspecting ACE.h5 shared timestamps: 1508307 test-only timestamps: 2 flight-only timestamps: 0 shared range: 442368366.1839997 to 898185969.1840003 test-only: 2 rows first rows: index=1478459, time=889231269.1840004 year month dom hhmm mjd secs destat de1 de4 pstat p1 p3 p5 p6 p7 anis_idx time ---- ----- --- ---- ----- ---- ------ ------ ---- ----- ------ ---- ---- ---- ----- -------- ----------------- 2026 3 7 40 61106 2400 0 2620.0 9.18 0 6640.0 22.4 1.81 0.38 0.112 -1.0 889231269.1840004 index=1478460, time=889231569.184 year month dom hhmm mjd secs destat de1 de4 pstat p1 p3 p5 p6 p7 anis_idx time ---- ----- --- ---- ----- ---- ------ ------ ---- ----- ------ ---- ---- ----- ----- -------- ------------- 2026 3 7 45 61106 2700 0 2440.0 10.3 0 6630.0 21.0 1.79 0.281 0.112 -1.0 889231569.184 flight-only: 0 rows ``` I have no good explanation for that (again, changes in the NOAA source data?) but overall this seems benign and an improvement in test. Besides that, no other diffs.

Runtime coercion existed, but UI shape assumptions still leaked across render paths and some background failures were effectively silent. This change tightens normalization boundaries so renderers consume stable state, and standardizes low-noise diagnostics for previously swallowed errors.

- **Feed/UI contract hardening**
  - Added `normaliseRenderState` in `shared/feed-controller.mjs` to enforce render-safe defaults (arrays, sets, counts, health/error objects, view mode/filter fields).
  - Updated `deriveView` to consume normalized state.
  - Updated render coordination (`app/boot/rendering.mjs`) to normalize once per render cycle before calling render modules.
  - Normalized `health` shape in `coerceLiveFeedPayload` to reduce downstream shape branching.

- **Consistent non-intrusive error diagnostics**
  - Added shared `reportBackgroundError(scope, message, error, context)` in `shared/logger.mjs`.
  - Supports optional `globalThis.BRIALERT_DIAGNOSTICS_HOOK` for observability without UI noise.
  - Replaced silent/swallowed paths with background reporting in:
    - `shared/persistence-ui.mjs`
    - `app/feed/source-requests.mjs`
    - `app/render/modal-remote-client.mjs`
    - `shared/modal-briefing.mjs`
  - Persistence save helpers now return boolean success (`true/false`) to make failure explicit at call boundaries while preserving current UX behavior.

- **Utility drift reduction + focused tests**
  - Removed duplicated note search tokenization by reusing shared `matchesAlertSearch` in `app/render/notes.mjs`.
  - Added targeted tests in `tests/decision-logic.test.mjs` for:
    - `normaliseRenderState` shape guarantees
    - `coerceLiveFeedPayload` health normalization
    - `matchesAlertSearch` tokenized AND semantics
    - persistence fallback/save-failure behavior
    - `cleanTextBlock`, `splitLongBriefSentences`, and diagnostics hook behavior

```js
// shared/logger.mjs
export function reportBackgroundError(scope, message, error = null, context = null) {
  const detail = error instanceof Error ? error.message : (error ? String(error) : '');
  debugLog(scope, message, detail || null);
  const hook = typeof globalThis?.BRIALERT_DIAGNOSTICS_HOOK === 'function'
    ? globalThis.BRIALERT_DIAGNOSTICS_HOOK
    : null;
  if (!hook) return;
  try { hook({ scope, message, detail, context }); } catch {}
}
```

body:
In a number of our parameterization regex patterns, we use lookaheads and lookbehinds to control when the pattern applies. There's theoretically a mechanism built into the `ParameterizationRegex` class for that: `lookahead` and `lookbehind` values can be set when defining the regex, and they'll automatically be included in the final pattern string. Most of our regexes which use lookaheads and lookbehinds don't use it, though, opting instead to include the lookahead or lookbehind directly in the pattern. Not only is this more explicit, it also accommodates patterns which need negative rather than positive lookaheads/lookbehinds, and patterns which need multiple lookaheads/lookbehinds.

This PR therefore switches the only two regexes using the attributes to also use explicit lookbehinds instead, and then deletes the now-unused attributes. No behavior changes here - just an attempt to make the code a touch simpler and more consistent.

This pull request introduces a new operator-driven simulation control panel to the dashboard, enabling live viewing and editing of simulated locomotive parameters. It adds a dedicated RTK Query API slice for simulator endpoints, defines types for simulated locomotives, and integrates the control panel UI into the dashboard layout. The changes are grouped below by theme.

**Simulator API and Types Integration**

* Added a new RTK Query API slice (`simulatorApi`) for managing simulated locomotives, including endpoints to get, create, update, and delete simulated locomotive records (`simulatorApi.ts`).
* Defined comprehensive TypeScript types for simulated locomotives and related request bodies, closely mirroring backend DTOs (`types/index.ts`).
* Registered the new `SimulatorLoco` tag type in the shared `baseApi` for cache management (`baseApi.ts`).
* Re-exported simulator API hooks and types for easy import elsewhere in the codebase (`index.ts`).

**Simulation Control Panel UI**

* Added a new `SimulationControlPanel` React component that displays and allows editing of simulation parameters (route, scenario, speed, etc.) for a selected locomotive. Edits are debounced and submitted as a single PATCH; scenario can be quickly set to "emergency" or reset to "normal" (`SimulationControlPanel.tsx`).
* Integrated the `SimulationControlPanel` into the dashboard grid, conditionally rendering it when not in replay mode (`DashboardPage.tsx`). body:
This is a minimal PR which simply adds such a flag. It gives no consideration to if any other code paths assume the old behavior, nor about any potential complex interactions between `first-party` and `audit-as-crates-io`. This also doesn't add tests to explore this behavior.

The point of this is to allow non-`crates.io` dependencies, prior assumed to be trusted, to now be declared as not trusted and instead tracked via `cargo vet`. This is necessary for any project which manages dependencies without using `crates.io` (and instead any alternative).

This concern was raised with https://github.com/mozilla/cargo-vet/issues/683. I just proceeded to poke at what an implementation could be.

I have locally tested this against my own project, which has just under 1000 dependencies and multiple Git repositories, and can confirm it appears to work as I wanted however. It lets me explicitly declare entries as non-first-party, confirm that against the output of `dump-graph`, and missing vet statements (and exemptions) for Git dependencies do in fact cause failures.

Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/72649045549333/task/1213965646075264

### Description
- Disable AI chat suggestions in fire tabs by introducing a `NilSuggestionsReader` that returns empty results, preventing chat history from being fetched or displayed in fire mode (iPhone, iPad, and unified input flows)
- Fix the "Fire tab" background info (empty content view) remaining visible when the user starts typing by reordering `updateURLFallbackForCurrentText()` before suggestion tray updates and adding `!shouldDisplaySuggestionTray` to the AI Dax visibility check during fade-out animation

### Testing Steps
<!-- Assume the reviewer is unfamiliar with this part of the app -->
1. Open a fire tab on iPhone and iPad
2. Tap the omnibar and switch to AI chat mode to begin editing
3. Verify no AI chat suggestions appear
4. Start typing a query in a fire tab — verify the background info / empty content view disappears and the suggestion tray is shown correctly
5. Switch to a regular (non-fire) tab — verify AI chat suggestions still appear as expected
6. On iPad, verify the chat history panel does not show suggestions in fire tabs but works normally in regular tabs

### Impact and Risks
Low: Minor visual changes, small bug fixes, improvement to existing features

#### What could go wrong?
- Reordering `updateURLFallbackForCurrentText()` before `suggestionTrayManager?.handleQueryUpdate` could introduce a visual flash — mitigated by keeping both calls within the same subscriber callback, so layout occurs in the same run loop


### Quality Considerations
N/A

### Notes to Reviewer
<!-- Anything specific you want reviewers to focus on -->
- `NilSuggestionsReader` is intentionally minimal (no-op pattern) to keep fire tab isolation simple and testable

body:
Add path canonicalization to `from_file_many` to mitigate path traversal vulnerabilities.

## Changes
- Canonicalize the path before opening in `from_file_many` using `Path::canonicalize()`
- Add security documentation warning callers to validate paths from untrusted sources

## Why
The `from_file_many` function opens files based on caller-provided paths. By canonicalizing the path before opening, any `..` components and symlinks are resolved to their actual absolute paths. This makes traversal attempts explicit rather than hidden in relative path components, reducing the risk of unintended file access when paths originate from untrusted sources.

## Semgrep Finding Details
The application builds a file path from potentially untrusted data, which can lead to a path traversal vulnerability. An attacker can manipulate the path which the application uses to access files. If the application does not validate user input and sanitize file paths, sensitive files such as configuration or user data can be accessed, potentially creating or overwriting files. To prevent this vulnerability, validate and sanitize any input that is used to create references to file paths. Also, enforce strict file access controls. For example, choose privileges allowing public-facing applications to access only the required files.

Semgrep Assistant generated this pull request to fix [a finding](https://semgrep.dev/orgs/sandboxaq/findings/715656322) from the detection rule [rust.actix.path-traversal.tainted-path.tainted-path](https://semgrep.dev/r/rust.actix.path-traversal.tainted-path.tainted-path).

body: ## Description The custom LLM provider modal was storing `api_key`, `api_base`, and `api_version` inside the generic `custom_config` dict, but the backend expects them as top-level fields (they have dedicated DB columns, SSRF protection logic, provider-specific transformations, and `api_key` uses encrypted storage). **Changes:** - **First-class field extraction (FE→BE):** On submit, `api_key`, `api_base`, and `api_version` are extracted from the key-value list and promoted to top-level fields in the API payload. Remaining entries stay in `custom_config`. - **First-class field seeding (BE→FE):** On edit, existing `api_key`, `api_base`, and `api_version` values are seeded back into the key-value list so they're visible and editable. - **Provider Configs description:** Updated to use `markdown()` with inline code and links to LiteLLM and Onyx docs. - **KeyValueInput cleanup:** Replaced `FieldMessage` with `ErrorTextLayout`, removed unused props (`disabled`, `onAdd`, `onRemove`, `onKeyValidate`, `onValueValidate`, `validateDuplicateKeys`, `validateEmptyKeys`, `name`, `fieldId`), removed stale `aria-describedby` refs, set `mode="fixed-line"` for the custom provider modal. Addresses: https://linear.app/onyx-app/issue/ENG-3942/fix-migration-for-custom-provider-configs-and-add-better-instructions. ## Screenshots + Videos ## Additional Options - [x] [Optional] Please cherry-pick this PR to the latest release version. --- ## Summary by cubic Extracts `api_key`, `api_base`, and `api_version` from the custom provider key-value list and sends them as top-level fields, fixing backend compatibility. Seeds these values back into the list when editing. Addresses ENG-3942. - **Bug Fixes** - Promote `api_key`, `api_base`, `api_version` to top-level in the submission payload; leave the rest in `custom_config`. - Seed existing top-level values back into the key-value list on edit. - Update “Provider Name” and “Provider Configs” help text using `markdown()` with inline code and links; set `KeyValueInput` to `fixed-line` in the modal. - **Refactors** - Simplified `KeyValueInput`: removed unused props and `FieldContext` ties; replaced `FieldMessage` with `ErrorTextLayout`; standardized validation to empty and duplicate keys. - Enhanced `EmptyMessageCard` with `sizePreset` ("main-ui" | "secondary") and optional `description`, and adjusted rendering. Written for commit bb3a7d9ba44a88d18d124b4b06b54ae3f5526c77. Summary will update on new commits.

author: kurousa
body:
🎯 **What:** The vulnerability fixed
Removed the use of `JSON.stringify` on the entire Strava activity object in the debug logs.

⚠️ **Risk:** The potential impact if left unfixed
Logging the full activity object or user-generated fields could expose sensitive geolocation PII (e.g., location names, precise routes) in the system logs, leading to a privacy breach.

🛡️ **Solution:** How the fix addresses the vulnerability
Updated the `Logger.log` statements to explicitly log only the `activity.id` (a non-sensitive identifier) instead of the whole object, completely mitigating the risk of PII leakage. The code was tested using `vitest` and no regressions were detected.

author: vilenarios
body:
## Summary

Major rewrite of the verify-sidecar with three goals: real cryptographic verification, ar.io brand alignment, and a simplified UX for non-technical audiences.

### Backend
- **RSA-PSS signature verification** via deep hash for ANS-104 data items and L1 transactions — proves data authenticity, not just hash consistency
- **Signature-first verification model**: signature is the primary proof, SHA-256 hash is a fallback fingerprint. Replaced the old tier system with 3 levels (Verified / Partially Verified / Pending) based on what was actually proved
- Independent SHA-256 hash always computed (even before gateway has digest)
- Gateway header extraction (owner, signature, trust signals, hops)
- Retry logic for unindexed transactions, partial results when /tx/ 404s but /raw/ available
- Cache expiry (30-day TTL), TX history lookup endpoint
- Raw data proxy for frontend image preview

### Frontend
- **ar.io brand kit**: colors (#5427C8, #DFD6F7, #23232D, #F0F0F0), Besley + Plus Jakarta Sans fonts, logo, favicon
- **Unified AuthenticityCard** replaces separate Owner + Integrity cards — one answer to "is this data authentic?"
- Provenance chain timeline, image preview, drag-and-drop file comparison
- Deep link support (?tx= param), curated examples (PDF/JPEG/PNG/Video)
- Copy-to-clipboard, Viewblock links, share button, honest progress indicator
- Jargon-free language: "Digital signature verified" not "RSA-PSS deep hash match"
- Dynamic base path (works at /verify/ and /local/verify/)

### Standalone deployment
- `deploy/` directory with docker-compose, nginx, start.sh
- One command: `bash deploy/start.sh`

## Test plan
- [ ] Verify a known indexed tx (e.g. `wfI-5PlYXL66_BqquCXm7kq-ic1keu0b2CqRjw82yrU`) → Level 3, signature verified
- [ ] Verify a tx with only wallet address (no pubkey) → Level 2, hash verified, signature skip reason shown
- [ ] Verify a brand new tx → retries, then partial or full result
- [ ] Try deep link: `?tx=WkaBoAfqfW2P4K2NO1SBDwhVsKQJSVTVEnaDvjoyZzA`
- [ ] Download PDF certificate and verify content matches UI
- [ ] Drag-and-drop file comparison on an image tx
- [ ] Re-verify button works
- [ ] UI renders correctly at `/local/verify/` path

author: larry-osakwe
body:
## Summary

Adds MCP server auth support to the Go SDK — composable HTTP middleware that works with **any** MCP library.

### What changed

- **`mcp.AuthInfoFromContext()`** and **`mcp.AccessContextFromContext()`** — context-based accessors so MCP tool handlers (which receive `context.Context`, not `*http.Request`) can retrieve auth info and delegated tokens
- **`examples/mcp-server-mcpgo/`** — complete example using [mcp-go](https://github.com/mark3labs/mcp-go)
- **`examples/mcp-server-official/`** — complete example using the [official MCP Go SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk)

### Design

The Go SDK is **MCP-library agnostic**. It provides composable HTTP middleware that works with any library that produces an `http.Handler`:

```go
mux := http.NewServeMux()
mux.Handle("/.well-known/", mcp.AuthMetadataHandler(...))
mux.Handle("/mcp", mcp.RequireBearerAuth(...)(yourMCPHandler))
```

No wrapper packages, no naming collisions, no coupling. Users bring their own MCP library and mux — Keycard handles auth and metadata.

### Why

Sean reported in #team-agent-dev that building an MCP server with the Go SDK results in 404s on `/mcp`. The SDK only provided auth primitives but no guidance on wiring them with an MCP transport library. The examples show the complete pattern for both popular Go MCP libraries.

## Test plan

- [x] `go vet ./mcp/...` — core package compiles
- [ ] Run mcp-go example, connect Cursor to `http://localhost:8080/mcp` — should get OAuth flow
- [ ] Docs PR: keycardai/docs#105

author: matt-pharr
body:
Summary

  - GitHub module installation: Unwires the previously disabled "Install GitHub" button — users can now paste a git-cloneable URL to install modules directly from GitHub
  - Bundled example modules: The examples/modules/ directory (N-Pendulum for Python and Julia) is now automatically surfaced in the module library, filtered by active kernel language, with a "Bundled" badge.
   These are read-only and always available without copying to the global store.
  - Project-local module storage: On import, module content is copied into <project>/modules/<module-id>/. On load, modules always resolve from the project directory first. This makes projects fully portable
   — zip a project folder and send it to someone who has never seen the module, and it just works.
  - Uninstall: Removes a module from the global store. Bundled modules cannot be uninstalled. Projects are unaffected since they have their own local copies.
  - Update: Modules with an upstream field (auto-set from GitHub clone URL, or declared in pdv-module.json) can check for updates via git ls-remote --tags (no clone needed) and re-install from upstream.
  Users must re-import to pick up changes in a project.

  Key design decisions

  - The global module store (~/.PDV/modules/packages/) is now a catalog only — it determines what's available to import, but projects never read from it at runtime
  - Module resolution order: project-local modules/ dir → global store → bundled examples
  - upstream is a new optional field in pdv-module.json pointing to a git-cloneable URL, enabling update checks for modules installed from disk that originally came from GitHub

  Test plan

- [x] Open Import Module dialog, paste a GitHub URL, verify module installs and appears in Library
- [x] Verify bundled N-Pendulum modules appear filtered by active kernel language with "Bundled" badge
- [x] Import a module, save project, verify <saveDir>/modules/<module-id>/ contains full module files
- [x] Copy a saved project to a new location, open it — verify module loads from project dir without global install
- [x] Import a module before first save, then save — verify pending module content is copied
- [x] Uninstall a module from Library, verify it disappears; confirm existing projects still work
- [x] Verify Uninstall is disabled for bundled modules and currently-imported modules
- [x] For a GitHub-installed module, click Update — verify it checks tags and reports status
- [x] Run a module action after import to verify scripts resolve from project-local path
